EVENT_NARRATIVE: Over two hundred swimmers were rescued by Volusia County Beach Patrol on September 4 alone. Around 1000 LST, two teenagers were caught in a rip current and rescued by bystanders. One of the teenagers was transported to a local hospital were she later died. Around 2000 LST, a 19 year old was found face down in the ocean after being trapped in a rip current. The victim was transported to a local hospital, where he remained in a coma.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure ridging south of the area lifted north to bring prevailing westerly winds on the 12th and 13th around to the southeast on the 14th. Afternoon seabreeze thunderstorms developed each day, with later timing on the 14th. Lightning from these scattered thunderstorms struck on individual and caused damage to trees. ||Moderate onshore flow caused strong rip currents near Upham Beach. A 16-year-old boy became caught in the current and was pulled out to sea. A 16-year-old girl then swam out to rescue him and also became caught in the current. The two were finally rescued by two surfers who reached them on their surf boards, but the foursome was then swept 150 yards offshore and were struggling to get back to the beach. Two girls on a jet ski then reached them and towed the four back to shore. The two swimmers were hospitalized.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Moderate onshore flow caused strong rip currents near Upham Beach. A 16-year-old boy became caught in the current and was pulled out to sea. A 16-year-old girl then swam out to rescue him and also became caught in the current. The two were finally rescued by two surfers who reached them on their surf boards, but the foursome was then swept 150 yards offshore and were struggling to get back to the beach. Two girls on a jet ski then reached them and towed the four back to shore. The two swimmers were hospitalized.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High seas, swells, and surf, produced by persistent southeast flow between high pressure in the eastern Gulf and low pressure in the lee of the Sierra Madre Oriental of northern Mexico maintained along shore currents at South Padre Island and perhaps rip currents near the Isla Blanca jetties (which focus wave energy) from July 12th through 13th.  On these days, offshore seas rose to between 6 and 8 feet, with a swell period nearing 7 seconds.  On the 14th, seas would begin dropping slowly falling to 5 to 6 feet with peak swell period dropping back to 5 or 6 seconds and an average period between 4 and 5 feet.||During the time when conditions were improving but still potentially hazardous, one person drowned in the surf along Isla Blanca Park.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A young man was found unconscious in the surf immediately offshore of Isla Blanca Park on South Padre Island during the mid to late afternoon of July 14th.  The man was likely a poor swimmer, and succumbed to either a rip current enhanced by water movement near the jetties.  While seas and surf had fallen to moderate levels - offshore seas had dropped below 5 feet and peak swell period was around 6 seconds - enough residual dangerous surf and current may have contributed to the death.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High waves caused an increased risk of rip currents along the lake-shore of southeastern Lake Michigan. An 11 year old boy was rescued by lifeguards at Silver Beach, but was not injured.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An 11 year old boy was rescued from the waters of Lake Michigan, off Silver Beach during the afternoon hours. The boy was taken out several yards away from shore before breaking free of the rip current. Two lifeguards rescued the boys and brought him to shore where he was found to have not sustained any injuries. No exact time was given other than this occurred in the afternoon.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High seas, swells, and surf, produced by the difference between relatively strong high pressure centered over Alabama and Mississippi and low pressure in the lee of the Sierra Madre Oriental of northern Mexico increased along shore currents at South Padre Island, along with rip currents near the jetties (which focus wave energy), during the day and evening of July 28th.  At daybreak, seas were still up near 7 feet along with a 7 to 8 second swell period and an average period above 5 seconds at the NOAA buoy around 60 miles northeast of the beach.  Seas continued between 5 and 6 feet during the day, with peak swell period running around 7 seconds.||A rip current aided by the east-southeast swell claimed the life of a man near the South Padre Island jetties near Isla Blanca Park during the late afternoon or early evening on the 28th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A local surfing instructor and trained spotter found a man unconscious in the water after hearing shouts from concerned family members. Though the victim was estimated to be a weak swimmer, moderate to strong rip currents likely caused the fatality, based on surf heights still 4 to 6 feet in the area, offshore sea heights 5 to 6 feet at the estimated time of death, and swell period of 6 to 7 seconds, all from a primary east-southeast swell.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A low pressure system that moved off the North Carolina coast on the 9th and combined with a high pressure system off the New England coast to start enhanced rip currents in Cape May County on the 9th. Conditions persisted through the weekend (10th and 11th) as a low pressure system formed on a cold frontal boundary. Spring tides were also occurring because of the new moon. Over the span of the three days, there were 277 rescues in Ocean City, 101 in Cape May (included hospitalization of one rescued swimmer) and and 15 in Cape May Point. A cold front moved through the state on the 10th and a low pressure system that rode along it in the western Atlantic helped the enhanced rip currents persist into the 11th. Conditions subsided on the 12th with the return of a weak high pressure system.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong southerly onshore winds produce deadly rip currents at the beaches of Alabama over the weekend.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Witnesses report a hispanic man reportedly went below the water around 3 PM CDT near tower 4 on the main public beach at Gulf Shores after struggling in a strong rip current.  His body was recovered by local search and rescue officials in the late afternoon hours.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Hurricane Irene passed by to the east of the Georgia coastline on August 26, 2011, producing beach erosion, high surf and rip currents across portions of southeast Georgia coast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lifeguards reported at least 15 rip current related rescues through the day on Tybee Island, Georgia.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A 19 year old swimmer walked to the end of the pier and jumped into the water where increasingly higher waves were observed. A combination of the strong current along the pier, increasing waves and 60 degree water all combined to cause problems for the novice swimmer. Officials located the body of the teen at 6:19 pm EDT 15 to 18 feet underwater.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Local media reported that St. Joseph dive team and Coast Guard officials were called to Silver Beach around 5 pm EDT. A 19 year old swimmer walked to the end of the pier and jumped into the water where increasingly higher waves were observed. A combination of the strong current along the pier, increasing waves and 60 degree water all combined to cause problems for the novice swimmer. Officials located the body of the teen at 6:19 pm EDT 15 to 18 feet underwater.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two men drowned in a rip current while attempting to save a six year old child.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two men, 41 year old Jeffrey Dinkins, and 42 year old Johnny Ward, died in a rip current while attempting to rescue a six year girl.  Two other people were involved and were rescued by an Horry County officer.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A marginally dangerous easterly swell, invitingly warm water temperatures, and focus around jetties on South Padre Island proved a dangerous mix during the evening of April 27th, when three young males with limited swimming experience ventured into the Gulf and were swept away from the coast by rip currents. One body was found later that evening, another found two days later, and the search was called off for the third after nearly a week.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Three young men from northern Mexico were swept to their deaths in dangerous rip currents near the Isla Blanca jetties on South Padre Island. The men took advantage of the warming surf temperatures to venture into the water, only to drown due to the strength of the current and a combination of lack of swimming ability in dangerous surf, and potential panic.  ||Conditions were ripe for rip currents.  A front had shifted winds to the north and northeast, and swell period increased to 8 and 9 seconds, with average period rising to 6.9 seconds at the NOAA Buoy about 35 NM east northeast of Port Mansfield. Surf heights were likely 4 to 6 feet, and the swell direction was from a favorable east-southeast direction.||The swimmers ventured out at around 6 PM.  A 22 year old was pulled out of the water during the mid evening and taken to Valley Baptist Medical Center, where he was pronounced dead.  An 18 year old was last seen in distress and unable to be rescued Wednesday evening; the Coast Guard found him early on the 29th at Boca Chica Beach, several miles south of the location where he entered the water.  A third victim, 12, was never found after several days of Coast Guard searches, which ended on May 1st.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Large easterly swells produced high surf along the northeast Florida coast as Hurricane Katia tracked north and well east of the coastal waters. Breakers ranged from 6 to 9 feet at times. Increased rip currents along the coast posed risk to beach goers.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Jacksonville Beach lifeguards had to rescue 6 swimmers during the day from rip currents.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Onshore flow along with elevated swell waves resulted in numerous rip currents along the Georgia coast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lifeguards reported 16 rip current related rescues were necessary at the Tybee Island, Georgia beaches.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Onshore flow along with elevated swell waves resulted in numerous rip currents along the Georgia coast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lifeguards reported 5 rip current related rescues were necessary at the Tybee Island, Georgia beaches.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Persistent onshore flow and large swells promoted greater than normal rip currents along the NE Florida Atlantic coast. A high surf advisory and a high risk of rip currents was in effect.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 20 year old male was rescued from rip currents at Jacksonville Beach. He was taken to the hospital. The swimmer was conscious after the rescue, which occurred near 8th Avenue North in Jacksonville Beach.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A 13 year old girl drowned at a beach near Surfside Texas. The drowning was believed to be related to rip currents.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Thirteen year old girl and a friend were caught in a rip current. The friend was rescued but the 13 year old drowned.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An east wind of 15 to 20 mph resulted in strong rip currents along the Atlantic beaches of the southeast Florida coast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 49 year old deceased male from Virginia washed ashore on November 28th at Juno Beach after being swept out to sea off Singer Island in a strong rip current on the 26th.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong southerly onshore winds produce dangerous rip currents at the beaches along northwest Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A Texas man who was pulled unconscious from the surf east of Portofino Island Resort on Pensacola Beach died after being airlifted to Gulf Breeze Hospital on Tuesday afternoon.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Long period swells associated with distant Tropical Storm Sean produced numerous strong rip currents along the east central Florida coast. A female swimmer was pulled out to sea by a rip current and battered by the rough surf so that she became submerged in water. Lifeguards pulled the woman from the water and performed CPR, but she was unresponsive and later pronounced dead at an area hospital.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 34 year old female tourist was caught in a rip current and pulled underneath the water during rough surf, causing her to drown. One other woman was also caught in a rip current while swimming, but she was pulled from the water and survived.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong east winds of 15 to 20 mph lead to the development of rip currents along the Atlantic coast beaches of South Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two teenage boys had to be rescued at Boynton Inlet from rip currents. One of the boys went into the water and began to be pulled away. His friend jumped in the water to rescue him, but both boys had to be pulled to shore by fire rescue personnel. They were taken to a hospital for treatment and later released.||The incident occurred after lifeguard hours.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A rip related fatality occurred at Myrtle Beach.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A young man drowned as a result of rip current in Myrtle Beach.  The fatality occurred at 24 Avenue North.  Two other individuals were caught in the rip but were rescued.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Atlantic high pressure provided for moderate to strong east winds along the southeast Florida coast, leading to the development of rip currents along the Atlantic beaches.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 78-year-old male Canadian tourist drowned as a result of rip currents at an unguarded beach in the 3100 Block of South Ocean Boulevard in Boca Raton, very close to the Palm Beach/Broward county line. The man was swimming with his girlfriend when she went out too far and got caught in a rip current. He rescued the woman, but had to be taken to the hospital and died the following evening.  ||The woman made it to shore and was hospitalized with a minor heart attack.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Onshore winds in combination with 3 foot long period swells, resulted in conditions favorable for rip current formation along the Georgia coast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Tybee Island lifeguards reported persistent rip currents throughout the day which resulted in 5 swimmers having to be rescued from the surf zone.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved through the area early in the morning, and caused moderate westerly flow behind the front. This caused strong rip currents at area beaches.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 16-year-old boy got caught in a rip current and was pulled well out to sea. Two beachgoers rescued the boy, and he was later transported by helicopter to the hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A father and son were rescued from rip currents at Vilano Beach. There was a low risk of rip currents that day.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A father and son were caught in a rip current for 45 minutes near Vilano Beach. Another son was on the beach and called for the help of two 13-year old surfers. The two surfers rescued the father and son. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A squall line formed well ahead of a cold front and moved through the area. The storms produced damaging winds and large hail.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 17 year old male was standing in chest-high water off of Treasure Island Beach and got caught in a rip current and drowned, while a severe thunderstorm also approached the area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two Eugene High School students on a school trip to the Pacific Ocean drown in the surf zone Saturday.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Three teenage boys were throwing footballs and frisbees on rocks jutting into the surf when the three were knocked into the surf by high waves. Two of the boys were drowned in the surf at Smelt Sands State Park near Yachats, Oregon.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Onshore flow over the Memorial Day weekend increased the risk of rip currents along the coast. Many rescues were performed.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Jacksonville Beach life guards had numerous rip current rescues on Memorial Day. Onshore flow combined with rough surf made for less than ideal beach conditions on the holiday.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong south winds ahead of an approaching cold frontal system resulted in strong rip currents along the beaches of northwest Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A Mobile resident died from drowning in a rip current in the surf off the Gulf Islands National Seashore as he pulled 3 other victims to safety.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High seas and strong southerly onshore winds produce dangerous rip currents over the weekend along the beaches of Northwest Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lifeguards had to pull more than 60 individuals caught in rip currents from the Gulf waters.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Breezy conditions were in place across the coastal waters with a moderate risk for rip currents in place. Several swimmers were rescued from the waters off of Honeymoon Island due to a strong rip current that developed near a jetty.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Five people swimming near a jetty got caught in a strong rip current and had to be rescued. A beach goer rescued two men before firefighters arrived and rescued another man and two women. The women were both 19-years-old, and the three men were ages 23, 40, and 50. Four of the five people were treated by paramedics at the scene. In addition, around 1 PM EDT, two other children caught in a rip current were rescued by the beach goer, but neither required medical treatment.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: On a late Saturday afternoon 4th of June, an incident occurred at the village of Amouli. Two young teenage girls were swimming close to the beach and were dragged out to the deep sea due to strong rip currents. One girl was rescued with minor injuries while the other girl���s body was never found. Rescue Team ended their search on the third day and later pronounced the 15 year old dead. The National Weather Service Office in Pago Pago issued a High Surf Advisory on Friday the 3rd of June and later canceled it on the 10th of June.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Moderate southeast winds led to the development of rip currents along the Palm Beach County coast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Four people were rescued by lifeguards in Lantana Beach during a one-hour span as a result of rip currents. Three of the four people were from the same family. Paramedics transported the victims as a precaution.||Time is estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A swimmer drowned when captured by a rip current off Galveston Island.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man drowned when he was taken under by a rip current off of Galveston. A woman swimming with the man was thrown onto a jetty and was injured but survived.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A woman was caught in a rip current and was rescued by lifeguards.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A woman got caught in a rip current near 1706 North Ocean Boulevard.  Two lifeguards rescued her and revived her using CPR. She was taken to a regional medical center for treatment.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A 12 year old boy swimming near the Packery Channel north jetty was caught in a rip current and drowned.  A separate rip current incident occurred later that day, in which two young girls and two men trying to rescue them were caught in a rip current south of Bob Hall Pier.  All four were able to make it safely back to shore, and were transported to local hospitals.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: East winds at Park Point were blowing at 10 to 20 mph then become light at 5 pm.  Two children nearly drowned when they were caught in a suddenly developing rip current.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The rip current suddenly developed about 515 PM CDT when light east winds shifted to west 15 to 20 mph, with gusts 25 to 30 mph.  Wind reports at Duluth International Airport, the Superior WI Bong Airport and the Sky Harbor Airport were used to obtain these directions and speeds.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A surfer who got caught in a rip current drowned in Virginia Beach.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A surfer who got caught in a rip current drowned near Croatan.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure across the eastern United States produced easterly winds and long period swells across the coastal waters of East Central Florida leading to the formation of moderate to strong rip currents. A male swimmer became caught in one of the stronger rip currents and was pulled underneath the water. A female surfer attempted to rescue the victim but could not locate him in the water. The body of the man was found early the next day.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 26 year old male swimmer was caught in a strong rip current and pulled underneath the water, causing him to drown. St. Lucie County Sheriff���s deputies found the man's body early the next morning. One other man was also caught in a rip current, but he escaped and survived.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The outer fringes of Tropical Storm Lee brought bands of strong showers and a few thunderstorms across the area, causing wind damage and rip currents.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A print media source reported that 50 people at Sand Key Beach were rescued by lifeguards from rip currents in the 24 hour period ending at 3:00 PM EDT on September 5.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A few rip current rescues occurred on Long Beach Island in Ocean County on the 12th, one near Barnegat Light and three in Long Beach Township. In all thirteen people were rescued. No serious injuries were reported. An onshore flow around a Canadian Maritimes high pressure system occurred on the 11th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A 15-year-old boy drowned after getting caught in a rip current near a jetty in Bradley Beach in Monmouth County during the late afternoon on the 9th. Two other people were also caught in the same rip current. A 28-year-old woman managed to pull herself onto the jetty while a 27-year-old man was rescued by two other men. The boy's body was recovered from the Shark River Inlet near the Ocean Avenue Bridge that separates Avon-By-The-Sea and Bradley Beach on the 14th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Persistent southeasterly flow driven by enhanced low pressure east of the Sierra Madre Mountains and High Pressure over the central Gulf of Mexico increased sustained winds and drove seas over 7 feet offshore, creating relatively rough and confused surf along South Padre Island, enhanced by the jetties at Isla Blanca Park.  The current took the life of a swimmer during the afternoon of June 17th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 66 year old man from Monterrey (state of Nuevo Leon) Mexico became in distress after being reportedly swept away from the Isla Blanca Park jetties on South Padre Island shortly after noon of June 17th.  The man was found about one half mile north of the jetties and brought to shore, but by the time paramedics arrived, was unresponsive.  After no revival after CPR was administered, the man was pronounced dead.||While the weather was sunny and hot, the water was disturbed.  Winds at offshore buoys ranged from 14 to 21 knots, with frequent gusts from 15 to as high as 27 knots through the day.  Seas at a NOAA Buoy about 50 nautical miles east northeast of Port Mansfield rising to 7.2 feet, with a 7 to 8 second swell period, from late morning through early afternoon.  Photos taken by a local surfing instructor showed estimated 2 to 3+ foot waves with choppy waters.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Rough seas developed on the southern coastal waters resulting in a forecast of a moderate risk of rip currents.  One man was caught in a rip current at Anthony's Beach in Dartmouth, Massachusetts and drowned.  Other beaches in the area reported numerous rescues and moderate rip currents on this day.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 42 year old man drowned after encountering a rip current at Anthony's beach in Dartmouth.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High waves on southeastern Lake Michigan cause rough conditions along the lake shore areas, where rip currents were common. One rip current at New Buffalo Public beach contributed to the death of 25 year old, plus minor injuries to a lifeguard. A second man was also caught by the rip current, but was rescued from a swim buoy and refused treatment.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Around 4:30 pm EDT, lifeguards on the New Buffalo public beach observed two men being pulled out by an apparent rip current. One of the men was able to grab onto a swim zone buoy. However his friend, a 25 year old man from Palos Hills, Illinois, was pulled out further into the lake. A lifeguard was able to rescue the man on the buoy, but waves as high as 12 feet prevented rescuers from reaching the other person. Eventually, a special Coast Guard boat able to handle the high waves, was called in and eventually found the 25 year old male's body floating along the shore. The other swimmer that was rescued refused medical treatment.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Rough surf and strong rip currents impacted the east-central Florida coast due to the passage of distant Hurricane Katia. A man drowned in a rip current at Daytona Beach while attempting to rescue his children who were being pulled seaward.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 40 year old male drown while attempting to rescue his children who were being pulled seaward by a strong rip current. The man was found floating in the water unconscious about a quarter mile away. Witnesses tried to perform CPR, and the man was taken to a local hospital, but didn't survive. ||The children were rescued by surfers.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A long fetch of north to northeast winds developed in the wake of a relatively strong early season cold front. These brisk winds resulted in long period swells impacting the east-central Florida beaches, which subsequently produced moderate to strong rip currents along the beaches. A man at Cocoa Beach, who was last seen on a flotation device, was pulled seaward by the rip currents. Medical responders performed CPR, but the man died a short time later at Cape Canaveral Hospital.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 29 year old man was caught in a rip current and drowned as he was pulled underneath the water.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A man was suspected of drowning in the ocean off the South Washington coast near the community of Seaview, Washington.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A group gathering on the beach approximately one mile south of Seaview,  Washington contacted Pacific County to report that a man had been in the water and was no longer in sight at 10:15 pm, Sunday. Pacific County launched two boats and the Coast Guard launched a boat and a helicopter to search for the man. The body was found the recovered the next day.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A Portland girl drowned Monday morning at Cape Lookout State Park on the Oregon coast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A nine-year-old girl from Southeast Portland was at Cape Lookout State Park on the North Oregon coast with a large family gathering. She and three other children were playing on a floatation toy in the surf about 30 feet from the shore. A wave swept the toy out from underneath them. As the children were returning to shore, a second wave hit them, taking the girl under the water. She was found several minutes later and taken to the hospital where she was pronounced dead.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong rip currents developed during the afternoon hours of August 28th.  Nine people attempted to go swimming at the Indiana Dunes State Park but the beach was closed due to the rip currents.  The people walked west to an unguarded beach at the Indiana Dunes National Lakeshore.  Around 400 pm CST, one of the nine people dissappeared about 200 feet from shore.  His body was recovered the next day.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Three to six foot waves caused some rip currents to develop along the shores of southeastern Lake Michigan. A 44 year old man was swimming at a beach near Coloma, Michigan where he drowned after being pulled out by the rip current.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast media reported a 44 year old male from Wheeling, Illinois was having trouble swimming at the beach off of Hagar Township Park. A woman with the swimmer lost sight of him and began yelling for help. Four minutes later rescuers arrived. He was in the water for approximately 90 minutes before a Coast Guard helicopter crew was able to recover his body.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A 24-year-old man drowned in Seaside Heights (Ocean County) near the Casino Pier after he was caught in a rip current shortly after 5 p.m. EDT on the 14th.  He was swimming with a 21-year-old woman when they became caught in the rip current. They were both struck by a wave. While the woman was pushed back to shore, the man was dragged farther out to sea. His body was found off the north side of the pier around 537 p.m. EDT and was pronounced dead a short time later.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Rough swells, set up by offshore seas of 4 to 5 feet with a period between 6 and 7 seconds, set up by persistent southeast winds of 15 to 18 knots with higher gusts well offshore, produced moderate rip currents along South Padre Island August 10th.  The currents are believed to have been a key reason for the first drowning in August and second of the summer.||The drowning was the sixth of 2011, five by rip or alongshore current. Each of the five was a resident of northern Mexico.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 44 year old man visiting from Monterrey, Nuevo Leon, Mexico was found face down in the surf just north of the Los Corales Condominiums north of Andy Bowie Park (8500 block of Padre Boulevard), near Public Beach Access Point 5. After attempts to revive the man were unsuccessful, he was pronounced dead either en route or after arrival at Valley Baptist Hospital in Harlingen.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A rip current caused a fatality at Rio Del Mar Beach.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man who was fishing Friday morning at Rio Del Mar Beach was carried out to sea by a Rip Current. The man was taken to a hospital where he was pronounced dead.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure over the Gulf of Mexico, interacting with a low pressure system and associated cold front moving through Texas, produced dangerous conditions in the near shore waters of South Padre Island on Christmas Day. Strong southerly winds around 20 knots and rough seas of 5 to 7 feet were observed for much of the day; the resulting longshore current swept a swimmer to his death on the north end of South Padre Island.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 44 year old man visiting from Missouri during the Winter Holidays drowned while swimming in dangerous longshore currents at Andie Bowie Park, which is maintained by Cameron County. This was the first and only rip or longshore current related drowning in 2012 on South Padre Island.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Northeast flow between 15-20 knots persisted between a wedge of high pressure north of the region and low pressure over the Atlantic. Conditions remained favorable through the day for rip currents along the southeastern Georgia coastline.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The media reported a 7 year old boy rescued from a rip current in the waters near 19th street. The boy was unconscious when pulled from the waters.  He was taken to the hospital and is in stable condition.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong rip currents developed causing a death and an injury.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 14 year old boy died after being caught in a rip current.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: On June 5th, an 18 year old black male drowned due to a rip current near the Seagrove area.  On June 7th, a 13 year old drowned due to a rip current near Miramar Beach at the Sandestin Golf and Beach Resort.  Red flags were flying in both cases.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: On June 5th, an 18 year old black male drowned due to a rip current near the Seagrove area.  On June 7th, a 13 year old drowned due to a rip current near Miramar Beach at the Sandestin Golf and Beach Resort.  Red flags were flying in both cases.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Beryl developed as a Subtropical Storm over the Atlantic Ocean well east of the North Coastal Georgia area. The cyclone eventually became a Tropical Storm and slowly moved to the southwest and finally made landfall along the northeast Florida coast. The system then weakened to a Tropical Depression and meandered about before slowly moving back to the northeast across coastal portions of Georgia and South Carolina. The system produced tropical storm force winds, rip currents, and areas of heavy rainfall across the region.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Forty-eight rip current related rescues for the day were reported on Tybee Island.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A swimmer near the south jetty of the Packery Channel on Padre Island became distressed in a rip current near the jetty. Rescue crews pulled the swimmer out of the water. But the lifeguards and paramedics were unable to revive the individual.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A young man was swimming near the south jetty of the Packery Channel on Padre Island. Rescue crews pulled the distressed swimmer out of the water. Lifeguards and paramedics attempted CPR at the scene but were unable to revive him. He was pronounced dead at the hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong currents due to Tropical Storm Debby caused a swimmer to drown in Orange Beach.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A swimmer drown in the waters off of Orange Beach due to strong currents caused by Tropical Storm Debby.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: West winds gusting to 20 mph produced considerable wave action on Northern Lake Michigan, and provided a favorable environment for rip currents.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A teenaged male from Portage, Michigan, drowned off of Cross Village Beach.  Dive teams were called in, and found the body about 40 feet from shore.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A man drowned near Nags Head after a rip current pulled him out to sea.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man drowned near Nags Head after a rip current pulled him out to sea.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Deep and strong easterly flow north of a low pressure area over the Caribbean Sea led to the formation of strong rip currents along the Atlantic beaches.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A male tourist in his 30s drowned after being caught in a rip current in rough conditions at the 77th Street beach in Miami Beach. The incident occurred after lifeguards had gone home for the day. The victim and a female friend were caught in the rip current, with the female getting out of the water and calling 911. Miami Beach Fire Rescue arrived on scene and two rescuers went to rescue the victim. The victim was taken to a local hospital where he was pronounced dead. ||One of the rescuers was tangled in rope on the way to help the victim and required medical attention at a hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Moderate east winds led to rip current formation along the beaches of Broward County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two swimmers, a 65-year-old man and 15-year-old girl, were rescued from rip currents by lifeguards along Fort Lauderdale Beach near Tower 13 at the 900 block of North Atlantic Blvd. Both were taken to the hospital and recovered.||A high risk of rip currents was in place for all of Southeast Florida, although Fort Lauderdale Ocean Rescue personnel were only flying yellow flags.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Sea breeze storms sparked a few strong storms over NE Florida during the evening.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 16-year old male drowned due to rip current at Fernandina Beach.  The time of death was approximated; a specific time during Friday afternoon was not given in the media report.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Northeast flow between 15-20 knots persisted between a wedge of high pressure north of the region and low pressure over the Atlantic. Conditions remained favorable through the day for rip currents along the southeastern Georgia coastline.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Tybee Island lifeguards reported 5 rescues so far as a result of rip currents near the pier.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong currents caused 3 swimmers to be pulled from the water at Pensacola Beach. One person died.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Pulses of northwest to northeast swells affected the Atlantic coastal waters and the Caribbean Passages. Seas were generally less than 7 feet.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 30 year old man drowned at the Vacia Talega beach in the municipality of Loiza.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong high pressure over the mid-Atlantic states caused breezy east winds over the southeast coast of the Florida peninsula with strong rip currents at the Palm Beach County beaches.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Four men had to be rescued from a strong rip current behind the Four Seasons Hotel at 2800 South Ocean Blvd in Palm Beach Florida. One man was taken to the JFK Medical Center where he was treated and released.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A low risk of rip currents was advertised due to subsiding swells and offshore flow.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lifeguards reported 4 rip current rescues at Jacksonville Beach that day with numerous rip currents sighted along the beach.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong rip currents developed causing a death and an injury.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 16 year old boy was caught in a rip current, listed in critical condition then later died in the hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: More frequent and stronger than average rip currents claimed the lives of two men and caused dozens of rescues along New Jersey beaches on the 20th. Both drownings occurred after lifeguards left for the day. In Asbury Park (Monmouth County), on the Second Avenue Beach, a 23-year-old male drowned late in the afternoon when he tried to save his sister who was stuck in  a rip current. His body was found approximately two hundred yards offshore. The sister was saved. Three other people were saved that day in Asbury Park after being pulled about 150 yards offshore. In Seaside Park (Ocean County), a 18-year-old male drowned after getting caught in a rip current off the O Street Beach, also late that afternoon. His body was recovered about one hundered fifty yards offshore the next day. There were three other rescues that day in Seaside Park and over thirty rescues just north in Seaside Heights (also in Ocean County). Other rip current rescues occurred in Bradley Beach (Monmouth County) and Perth Amboy (Middlesex County).
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong east wind produced dangerous rip currents at the beaches along the Atlantic Coast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two swimmers were rescued from a rip current at MacArthur Beach State Park and taken to the Palm Beach Gardens Medical Center. The state park does not have guarded beaches.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A 10-year-old boy who was swimming with his family drowned after getting caught in a rip current with his sister in the beach near Martin Luther King Boulevard in Atlantic City (Atlantic County) during the evening of the 10th. His sister was rescued from a jetty. His body was found on the 13th in Margate (Atlantic County). No lifeguards were on duty.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 43 year old male drowned while attempting to help swimmers caught in a rip current near the Shoals Club on Station House Way.  Rescue teams from Bald Head Island pulled seven people to safety but could not locate the 43 year old victim.  Rescue personnel pulled his body from the water about an hour after the incident started.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A 24-year-old man drowned after believed to have been caught in a rip current in Bradley Beach (Monmouth County) and was pronounced dead at 7 p.m. EDT on the 29th.  He drowned while swimming south of a jetty in the waters off of Brinley Avenue Beach in Bradley Beach. Around the same time, four teenagers were also caught in the same rip current, but made it back to shore.  They were hospitalized for observations. This was the second rip current related drowning in Monmouth County this week.  Both incidents occurred on unguarded beaches in locations known to have rip currents.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Tybee Island lifeguards reported 8 rescues due to rip currents near the pier. Two people were injured on the jetties.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A man was caught up in a rip current and drowned in Virginia Beach.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was caught up in a rip current and drowned in Virginia Beach.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A storm in the central, north Pacific sent a large, long-period west swell into the Southern California coastal waters from the 2nd through the 3rd, causing surf of 5 to 8 feet with max sets 10-14 feet along the Orange and San Diego County beaches. Only minor damage was reported in Orange County, however one fatality did occur.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: During the swell increase on Monday the 2nd, a 26-year-old male and his friend were swept out past the surf zone in a strong rip current at Huntington Beach. The man's friend was pulled to safety by a nearby beach-goer, but did not want to come in himself. It took a helicopter two hours to recover his body, but by that time he had died.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A 27 year old male drowned near the M.B. Miller County Pier in Bay County, FL around 12:30 pm CDT on Sunday, April 1, 2012.  A witness told police that the man was in the Gulf about chest deep and believed he may have been caught in a rip current.  At least two other rescues occurred that day with no injuries.  Yellow flags were posted at the beach.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An east wind along the Florida east coast resulted in strong rip currents at the beaches.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 60 year old man was rescued from a rip current by the Fort Lauderdale Fire Rescue. The man was swimming at an unguarded beach along Galt Ocean Drive. He was taken to a nearby hospital.||A total of eight people were rescued from rip currents by Fort Lauderdale Fire and Ocean Rescue as of late afternoon.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: A father and his three teenage children were rescued from rip currents while swimming at the beach on Singer Island and taken to St. Mary's Medical Center as a precaution.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An east wind along the Florida east coast resulted in strong rip currents at the beaches.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A family of five was rescued from rip currents by the city of Hollywood lifeguards. Time is estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Onshore winds with gale-force gusts, accompanied by waves reported to be at least 4 to 5 feet high were occurring throughout the afternoon and evening of July 18th.  Three young women, age 12, 13, and 13, were caught in a powerful rip current, and one of the women, Mia Ojanen, 12, had to be rescued about 4:42 PM CDT.  The other two had a very close call with being drowned in the rip current.  Specifically, at nearby Pier 20, near the Blatnik Bridge, winds were east-northeast, measured at 38 mph, gusting to 45 mph at 2:35 PM CDT and 35 mph, gusting to 42 mph at 5:20 PM CDT.  At the nearby Sky Harbor Airport, protected by a tall stand of trees upwind, reported 29 knot (33 mph) northeast winds, gusting to 35 knots (40 mph) were measured at 1:54 PM on July 18th. EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast media and a local newspaper reported several rip current rescues and one drowning along the coast of Broward County during the afternoon. Fort Lauderdale Fire Rescue responded to a husband and wife getting caught in a strong rip current at an unguarded beach at 4200 Galt Ocean Drive at about 1:30 PM EDT. They were transported to Holy Cross Hospital with life threatening injuries where the 80-year old woman was responsive but her 83-year old husband was not. He was later pronounced dead. Two men and a woman, ages unknown, were rescued from a rip current just north of Hallandale Beach. The men were transported to Aventura Hospital but the woman refused treatment.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong area of high pressure located across the Atlantic resulted in onshore winds along the southeast coast of Florida and strong rip currents at the beaches.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man, unknown age, nearly drowned at Ocean Reef Park in Riviera Beach and was taken to St. Mary's Medical Center late Thursday with injuries that were considered life-threatening.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure over the Atlantic resulted in an onshore flow across southeast Florida with strong rip currents at the beaches during the weekend of July 6 and 7. Dozens of people were rescued at southeast Florida beaches.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Palm Beach County Fire Rescue responded to a call around 5:37 PM EDT that as many as six swimmers were caught in a strong rip current. Upon arrival, rescue crews discovered that there were a total of four swimmers and an unknown number of rescuers. The four swimmers had already been rescued by bystanders and left the scene. One adult male, however, had been caught in a rip current helping to rescue young swimmers at Kreusler Park and was transported to JFK Medical Center in critical condition.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure over the Atlantic produced onshore winds along the southeast coast with strong rip currents developing at the beaches.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 23-year old male drowned in a strong rip current at Fort Lauderdale Beach trying to save six of his friends when they were caught in the current. It occurred during the early evening after lifeguards had left for the day and the seven friends did not heed the red flag warnings lining the beaches. Lifeguards had saved 41 people on Sunday in the same location.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The northern extent of a weak tropical wave over the northwest Bahamas produced breezy onshore winds along the southeast Florida coast with dangerous rip currents at the beaches.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Strong rip currents occurred during the day along the Atlantic beaches with about 50 rescues reported by Miami Beach Ocean Rescue. An elderly man and woman were pulled from the water by Ocean Rescue lifeguards at Allison Park near 64th Street and Collins Avenue. They were rushed to Mt. Sinai Medical Center but doctors were unable to save them.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The northern extent of a weak tropical wave over the northwest Bahamas produced breezy onshore winds along the southeast Florida coast with dangerous rip currents at the beaches.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 17-year old male was found under water at Dubois Park in Jupiter after being caught in a rip current. He was taken to a local hospital and his condition is not known.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Frequent gusts of 25 knots with 4 to 6 foot seas produced Rip Currents at Fripp Island. 3 people died due to drowning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Four people were caught in the rip current at Fripp Island, and a 14 year old girl became separated from the others and swam back to shore and called for help. A 16 year male was found drowned later on July 14; a 38 year old male was later found drowned on July 15; the third body of a 17 year old male was found July 17.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Southeast winds and a southerly swell produced strong rip currents over much of coastal Brunswick County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Numerous rip current rescues occurred over much of the beaches of Brunswick county.  There were 3 fatalities, one at Ocean Isle Beach, and two at Sunset Beach.  Three other people were hospitalized.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Numerous to widespread thunderstorms developed over the area as several mid level shortwaves ejected northeast over a stationary front between an inland upper trough and high pressure offshore. Tropical air featuring PWATs over 2 inches and repeating thunderstorms produced torrential rain and several reports of flash flooding across the Charleston Tri-county region. A couple of thunderstorms became severe with damaging wind gusts and heavy rainfall during the afternoon. Two storms exhibited sufficient rotation to prompt Tornado Warnings.  Persistent onshore winds and long period swell also led to a moderate risk of rip currents along the coast.  One rip current resulted in a drowning while an individual tried to rescue another person already in a rip current.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: One person drowned trying to rescue another person in a rip current.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A pair of drownings occurred off Panama City Beach on July 20th, which were separate events. One of the drownings included a former Auburn Univ basketball player and received some news reporting. Multiple rescues were also reported. Bay county was flying Double Red flags at the time, and the NWS had a high risk in effect.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Tybee Island lifeguards reported numerous ongoing rip currents resulting in 3 rescues and 9 assists during the day.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A man vacationing with his family at Topsail Beach got caught in a rip current and drowned.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A Greensboro man vacationing with his wife and children drowned due to a rip current near the 900 block at the south end of Topsail Beach, about 500 feet from where he initially went into the water. A moderate risk for rip currents was forecast at the time.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A inexperienced swimmer at an unguarded beach was caught in a rip current and drowned.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 22 year old male tourist from New York became caught in a rip current and drowned. He was an inexperienced swimmer. Two others, a male and female, were also caught in the rip current, but were better swimmers and they escaped to safety. The nearest lifeguard tower was approximately 5 miles away.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A 30-year-old Georgia man died after being caught in a rip current in Ormond Beach south of Cardinal Avenue.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Multiple media sources reported a 30-year old Georgia man drowned after being caught in a rip current, south of Cardinal Avenue in Ormond Beach. An off-duty lifeguard was in the area and pulled the man from the Alantic. Another woman who was trapped in the rip current was rescued.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A 25 year old male was transported to the hospital and later died after being pulled from the water during the afternoon hours behind the Legacy by the Sea Resort, located near the 15000 block of Front Beach Road.  Strong rip currents were in the area with single red flags flying.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A 22 year old male drowned in a rip current on Frisco Beach.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: A person was dragged by a rip current. He was rescued later.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A ridge of high pressure over the eastern U.S. caused an east wind along the Florida east coast of 15 to 20 mph. This led to the formation of dangerous rip currents at the beaches along the northern coast of Palm Beach County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Several swimmers had to be rescued during the afternoon and early evening at the beaches along the coast of northern Palm Beach County, some nearly drowning. ||The first report was just after 2 pm EDT at Ocean Cay Park in Jupiter where two people nearly drowned. They were pulled from the water and both were taken to Jupiter Medical Center where one was reported in critical condition. Around 445 PM, six other swimmers were also rescued from the dangerous rips in the same area with one was taken to Jupiter Medical Center. ||Around 6 pm EDT, two male swimmers struggled in the waves at Lake Worth Pier but managed to reach shore and declined further treatment. ||The last reported rescues were shortly after 7 pm EDT when eight other swimmers were caught in rip currents in two separate incidents off the Lake Worth Pier. Six of the swimmers nearly drowned and were taken to Bethesda Memorial Hospital in Boynton Beach and JFK Medical Center in Atlantis.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure over the southeast states produced an east wind along the Florida Atlantic coast of 10 to 15 mph and moderate rip currents.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Palm Beach Post reported a woman was pulled from the surf at the Lake Worth Beach due to a possible rip current. The woman did not require CPR but was taken to the JFK Medical Center in Atlantis for follow-up treatment.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Stronger winds associated with passing scattered thunderstorms combined with strong outgoing astronomical tides produced a series of deadly rip currents along the Gulf-side beaches of Alabama on Sunday June 9th and Monday June 10th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Strong rip currents developed as winds increased around scattered thunderstorms combined with strong outgoing tidal currents.  Three vacationing swimmers just off the Gulf-side beaches of the Fort Morgan Peninsula became caught in strong rip currents and drowned.  The swimmers were reportedly vacationing separately from Bowling Green, Kentucky, Bossier City, Louisiana, and Overland Park, Kansas.  One of the victims was reportedly trying to rescue another victim.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Stronger winds associated with passing scattered thunderstorms combined with strong outgoing astronomical tides produced a series of deadly rip currents along the Gulf-side beaches of Alabama on Sunday June 9th and Monday June 10th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A vacationing swimmer from Jonesboro, Arkansas became caught in a strong rip current near Gulf Shores and drowned.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A male was killed in the surf zone. The cause was unknown.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The media reported a drowning about 1 mile or less from the St. Mary River inlet. The cause of drowning death was either due to tidal currents or rip currents.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Persistent onshore winds of 10 to 15 knots helped create favorable conditions for rip currents.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A Clearwater woman drowned in the Gulf of Mexico on her birthday five blocks north of the Clearwater Pier. Her husband reported deep water and strong currents.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong rip currents caused the drowning of two people at Myrtle Beach.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Strong rip currents pulled two people out to sea.  A teen got caught in a rip current near 48th Ave N, and another man who tried to rescue the boy was also pulled out from the rip current.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A persistent southeast wind and swell produced strong rip currents at North Myrtle Beach.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Strong rip currents caused a man to drown at 15th Avenue South in Myrtle Beach.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Gusty northwesterly winds moved across Lake Michigan in the wake of a strong cold front. Wave heights of three to six feet were common during the afternoon hours of the 27th. A 15 year old boy from Illinois was caught in a rip current and pulled away from shore. He was rescued and airlifted to a Chicago hospital, where he died several hours later.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 15 year old boy was roughly 100 feet offshore from a New Buffalo public beach when he was caught in a rip current.  The rip current pulled him away from shore. Lifeguards quickly noticed the problem and were able to rescue the boy and perform CPR. He has transported to a local hospital and then airlifted to a Chicago hospital, where he died later that evening.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A rip current fatality occurred at Huguenot Memorial Park on Fort George Island which was an unguarded beach.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A male was killed from a rip current. The time of the incident was unknown and entered at 16:00 EDT for inclusion of the event in StormData.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 65 year old male from Baton Rouge Louisiana drowned after he was pulled out into the gulf by a rip current. The incident occurred at Navarre beach.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two men were caught up in rip currents and drowned in Ocean City.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 52-year-old male died after being overtaken by a rip current in Ocean City.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two men were caught up in rip currents and drowned in Ocean City.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 34 year old male from Montgomery, AL was caught in a rip current and swept out about 80 feet from the beach and drowned. The drowning occurred at the Cotton Bayou beach access in Orange Beach.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Moderate northeast winds and swells along the Palm Beach County coast in the wake of a cold front led to rip currents at the county beaches.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man nearly drowned from apparent rip currents at the Boynton Inlet. Fire rescue crews responded to a call of a reported drowning, and found a man breathing and conscious.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Rip currents on the north coast of Tinian claimed the life of a young U.S. Marine.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 26 year old Marine from the Marine Wing Communication Squadron 18 based in Okinawa, Japan, was taking part in Exercise Valiant Shield and Forager Fury on Tinian. He went into the ocean on the northwest side of Tinian to cool off.|It was reported that he was swept over the reef. He may have been caught in a rip current. After a few days search by Saipan DPS, U.S Navy and Coast Guard crews he was presumed lost.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A moderate risk of rip currents was in effect due to lingering swells of 2-5 ft and periods of 11-14 seconds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was caught in a rip current at Mickler's Landing. His body was recovered and the  cause of death was determined to be drowning due to a rip current.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Moderate east to southeast winds led to rip current formation along the southeast Florida coast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A young man (Jacobo Dorcely) drowned while swimming at Hammock Park near Boynton Inlet. The man's age was not indicated in media reports, but is estimated to be around 18 years of age. His body was recovered about 50 feet from shore. Occurred at an unguarded beach.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Building high pressure over the Atlantic resulted in onshore flow along the Florida east coast and rip currents at  the beaches.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast media reported that a 27-year old male was pulled out to sea from a rip current. The Coast Guard has suspended the search and the man is presumed dead.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High Surf conditions due to north to northwest swells affected the north coast of Puerto Rico from November 3rd to November 6th, 2014. Seas between 7 to 9 feet with breaking waves of around 12 to 16 feet were observed. Dangerous Rip Current were also observed.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 51 year old man was drowned at Condado Beach in San Juan.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A large, long period northerly swells of 7 to 9 feet affected the Atlantic waters. A high surf advisory and coastal flood advisory were in effect for the north facing coasts of Puerto Rico and U.S. Virgin Islands. A small craft advisory was also in effect for all the waters.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 59-year old male tourist from California died while snorkeling at Ensenada beach.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure north of the region provided a moderate northeast to east wind flow across the south Florida area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 19-year-old man was caught in a rip current while swimming at an unguarded beach near Boynton Inlet at Ocean Inlet Park. The teen swam back to shore before rescue boats reached the area, and was treated at a local hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Swell from Tropical Storm Faxai caused one drowning death on Guam.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Tropical Depression 03W formed 350 miles southeast of Guam on the 28th of February. By the morning of the 1st of March, the depression gained strength and became a tropical storm.  Tropical Storm Faxai passed 345 miles east of Guam on the morning of March 4th.||Even though the storm passed far to the east of Guam, the combination of wind produced by Faxai and enhanced gradient wind flow north of the storm generated large swells. These swells produced |hazardous surf and high rip currents along east and north facing reefs of Guam. These perilous conditions claimed the life of a women on Tuesday, March 4th.  Around 330 pm that day, the Guam Fire |Department received a 911 call. A 74 year old Japanese tourist was pulled from the waters of Tumon Bay. She was found submerged in the waters, between the Guam Reef Hotel and the Westin Resort. ||She was rushed to Guam Memorial Hospital (GMH) with medics performing CPR on her en route. The lady was in critical condition and remained on life support until she died on the morning of the 6th. The GMH Nursing Supervisor said that the woman was pronounced dead at 4:30am.||A High Surf Advisory was in effect when the incident occurred.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong storms over the Northwest Pacific continued to create hazardous surf and strong rip currents across the Marianas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: On January 20th 2014 Guam Fire Department received a call around 11:48 am. Dwight Artero McKeever and his wife Sandra were about to walk on Ypao Beach in Tumon when they noticed a swimmer in distress. We paused for a 	minute to look, and we noticed a lady who was flailing her hands in panic said McKeever. Seeing a group of boys skimboarding nearby, McKeever began whistling loudly to get their attention|pointing to the woman behind them. She was about 30 to 40 feet from shore at the time. 	At the same time Ypao Beach lifeguards saw the woman go under the water and immediately responded.  McKeever began running to the woman as the boys swam to her. Hoisting her head out of the water, McKeever began to swim the woman back to shore. the boys carried her legs. Once the woman was brought to shore    	McKeever, a former certified lifeguard, began to perform CPR on the lady. Lifeguard Robert Miranda says fellow lifeguards Joe Nauta and Stephan April continued to perform CPR and rescue breathing on the woman before she was revived about three minutes later. 	The woman was breathing on her own when paramedics arrived. Devan Mendiola was one of the young men who help rescue the woman. The woman was 36 years old and is from Korea. |     Lifeguard Robert Miranda said ���I think she was swimming off the shore line but the water conditions with the swell coming in there's strong currents pulling people down to deeper waters,���.The lady was in stable condition in the Emergency Room at Guam Memorial hospital as of 5:20pm according to GMH Public Information Officer June Perez.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Swell generated from a storm system north of the Marianas generated strong rip currents across the Marianas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: On the morning of December 1st, a 23 year old Air Force Airman, Alec Dye, was reported missing. He was last seen at Tarague Beach, which is near the northern tip of Guam. It was thought that he entered the water at the beach at around 4:45 am that morning.||Over the course of the next several days a search for Dye was conducted. Employed in the effort to find the airman were Navy helicopters, a 110 foot Coast Guard patrol boat, members of the Andersen AFB Fire Department, AAFB security, Guam Fire |Rescue and Police Department members as well as 60 volunteers from Andersen Air Force Base. ||A few days later, on the morning of the 4th, an Andersen Air Force Security Patrol found the airman's remains. They were close to where it was estimated that he entered the water. A high surf advisory was in effect at the time. Hazardous surf of |7 to 10 feet was predicted for north facing reefs at the time. Data for the Ritidian buoy showed swell periods of around 13 seconds at the time. Dye may have gotten caught in strong rip currents caused by the swell and high surf.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A 21 year old man drowned in high surf and strong rip currents near Navarre Beach, FL.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 21 year old man from Louisiana drowned due to high surf and strong rip currents near Navarre Beach, FL.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Breezy onshore winds along the Atlantic coast resulted in strong rip currents at the beaches.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: WSVN news reported two swimmers were rescued by Miami-Dade Fire Ocean Rescue from a strong rip current at Haulover Beach near 138th Street and Collins Avenue. One swimmer was treated at the scene and a male swimmer was unresponsive in the water. Ocean Rescue pulled him out, started CPR and he was transported to the hospital with non-life-threatening injuries.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure over north Florida produced a moderate east to southeast wind flow across the area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Five people were rescued from rip currents at an unguarded beach north of Dania Beach Pier. A man and a women, both in their 20s, were taken to a local hospital for observation. Time is estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Active rip currents spawned several rescues. One was a near drowning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A near drowning occurred from a rip current at Little Talbot Island. The person was rescued.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Active rip currents spawned several rescues. One was a near drowning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Three rescues occurred due to rip currents.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A teen from Lakewood drowned on the 14th off Sunset Beach. Damian Frierson Jr., 19, was pulled from the water by Huntington Beach city lifeguards and transported to Huntington Beach Hospital, where he died around 1821 PST, according to the Orange County coroner. It took about 25 lifeguards, 15 from the city and additional units from Bolsa Chica State Beach and Seal Beach, about 47 minutes to locate Frierson, who was found submerged in about 10 to 15 feet of water. At about 1643 PST, a lifeguard on duty told Frierson and two women with him to get out of the water because of the currents. A guard saw one of the women on shore yelling that her friends needed help and that he other woman was still in the rip current. CPR was initiated after Frierson was brought back to shore. It was the first drowning in Huntington Beach and Sunset Beach this year. EVENT_NARRATIVE: One lifeguard were knocked off their feet due by a rip current/ large shore break wave at Bethany Beach during a training exercise. A right ankle injury and a lost tooth occurred due to the fall.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A swimmer was rescued from a rip current, and was resuscitated on the beach. The victim was in stable condition when taken to the hospital.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A swimmer was rescued from a rip current, and was resuscitated on the beach. The victim was in stable condition when taken to the hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Tropical Storm Colin made landfall across the southeast big bend during the overnight hours of June 6-7.  Damage was relatively minor across the region.  ||In Leon county, seven roads were closed on Monday afternoon due to flooding.  Three were main roads, including Weems Road, North Meridian, and near Lake Ella.  Localized rainfall amounts around 10 inches occurred in eastern Leon county.  ||In Franklin county, a voluntary evacuation was in place along the coast.  Coastal flooding affected areas from Apalachicola to Alligator Point.  Homes had water in backyards on the Gulf side of US-98 from Carrabelle Beach to St Teresa Beach.  The St Teresa Beach and boat ramp flooded.  Alligator Point Road was flooded with debris washed inland.  Gulfshore Drive was flooded and closed on the east end of Alligator Point.  ||In Wakulla county, coastal flooding was reported in Mashes Sands Beach, Panacea, and Saint Marks.  Flooding was greatest in St Marks.  Several roads in the area were closed around high tide with two businesses getting water inside.  Riverside Cafe had 1 foot of water enter the structure, and Cooter Stew had 3 to 6 inches of water enter the structure.||In Taylor county, the beaches reported 1 to 2 feet of inundation with locally higher values on Monday afternoon.  This included Dark Island, Cedar Island, Keaton Beach, Dekle Beach, and Ezell Beach.  The town of Steinhatchee had numerous roads flooded due to storm surge that started at 1:30 pm and ended around 6 pm.  Homes were surrounded by flood waters, but no water made it inside.  ||In Dixie county, 1.5 to 2 feet of inundation occurred in Horseshoe Beach and Suwannee, mainly right along the waterfront.  Storm surge was observed moving up the Suwannee River as far north as the US-19 gauge at Wilcox, FL.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Tropical Storm Colin produced long period swell, rough surf, and numerous rip currents along the Alabama beaches from late Sunday, June 5th, through Tuesday night, June 7th. A rip current fatality occurred on Tuesday, June 7th in Baldwin County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A male swimmer from Texas was rescued from the water after being caught in a rip current. First responders were not able to revive him. There were a total of 9 water rescues in Orange Beach on Tuesday.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Long period swell from distant Typhoon Haima. Caused dangerous rip currents across the Marianas.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: On the morning of the 21st of October around 7:30 a.m. a man in his late 40s was|pulled from the water near Sheraton Laguna Guam Resort in Tamuning. After the man was taken from the water CPR was performed on him on route to the hospital. The man survived.||On the 22nd of October, two people were found face down by fishermen in the water off of Ritidian Point at around 10:35 a.m.. Both were tourist from South Korea visiting the island. One person was a male of 31 years old and the other a female of 27 years of age. ||At the time of the incidents, there were no watches, or advisories out for hazardous|surf. Long period west swell from distant Super Typhoon Haima was impacting the area. Data from Ritidian Buoy indicated a swell between 12 to 18 seconds from the west. While the maximum surf generated by the swell probably was only 5 feet, the long period of the swell could have produced some rip currents.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Tropical Storm Colin produced long period swell, rough surf, and numerous rip currents along the western Florida Panhandle Beaches from late Sunday, June 5th, through Tuesday night, June 7th. A rip current fatality occurred on Tuesday, June 7th in Okaloosa County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 36 year old male from Georgia was caught in a rip current near the Okaloosa Pier and drowned.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Moderate rip currents were observed during the late afternoon hours of June 4th. As a result of the rip currents, two youngsters entered the water and got caught in  a rip current. The kids father was able to rescue them but then collapsed and died upon returning to shore due to a heart attack. The man was 55 years old and the estimated time of death was about 4:45 pm. This death is deemed indirect.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Moderate rip currents were observed during the late afternoon hours of June 4th. As a result of the rip currents, two youngsters entered the water and got caught in  a rip current. The kids father was able to rescue them but then collapsed and died upon returning to shore due to a heart attack. The man was 55 years old and the estimated time of death was about 4:45 pm. This death is deemed indirect. The rip current risk was low for the day though beach replenishment projects may have created more rips on that day.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A 24 year old women and her male companion were knocked off their feet by a rip current and pulled into the ocean off of the Spray beach section in Long Beach Township NJ at around 11 am. The women died less than a day later.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 24 year old women and her male companion were knocked off their feet by a rip current and pulled into the ocean off of the Spray beach section in Long Beach Township NJ at around 11 am. The women died less than a day later.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two people were hospitalized due to injuries on 6/25 from a rip current. This occurred at Bethany Beach.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two people were hospitalized due to injuries on 6/25 from a rip current. This occurred at Bethany Beach. Time of day unknown.
