EVENT_NARRATIVE: A Tybee Island lifeguard confirmed 1 drowning from a rip current off of Tybee Island Beach.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong high pressure building from the north and offshore low pressure helped produce a strong northeast wind ahead of an approaching full moon. These conditions produced an elevated risk of rip currents along the Southeast Georgia coast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Tybee Ocean Rescue reported approximately 18 rescues over the course of the day off Tybee Island Beach.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong high pressure building from the north and offshore low pressure helped produce a strong northeast wind ahead of an approaching full moon. These conditions produced an elevated risk of rip currents along the Southeast Georgia coast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Tybee Ocean Rescue reported numerous rip currents occurring along all portions of the Tybee Island coastline with several rescues required.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong high pressure building from the north and offshore low pressure helped produce a strong northeast wind ahead of an approaching full moon. These conditions produced an elevated risk of rip currents along the Southeast South Carolina coast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Folly Island lifeguards reported 2 rip currents and 2 rescues at Folly Beach. One rip current was ongoing and approximately 10 yards wide and 50 yards long.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong high pressure building from the north and offshore low pressure helped produce a strong northeast wind ahead of an approaching full moon. These conditions produced an elevated risk of rip currents along the Southeast South Carolina coast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Isle of Palms Fire Department rescued 3 adults and 1 child on the northern end of Isle of Palms Beach. One person was taken to the hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A northeast/east wind behind a departing cold front helped produce a few rip currents along the Southeast South Carolina coast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A rip current was observed near 34th Avenue and required the rescue of at least one person.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Although high pressure was building into the region on Friday, residual southerly long period swells resulted in a moderate threat for rip current development. This unfortunately resulted in a rip current related drowning of a young male at Coopers Beach late Monday afternoon.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Tom Surdyke, 18, from Missouri died on Tuesday night June 28, after fighting for his life at Stony Brook Hospital. The West Point cadet was pulled, unresponsive, from the ocean at Coopers Beach in Southampton Village on Friday afternoon June 24th.  Mr. Surdyke was a cadet at West Point military academy.||According to a female eyewitness, Mr. Surdyke and another individual got caught in a rip current.  She said the two men were on a sandbar when one screamed for help, as he held Mr. Surdyke up out of the water. The eyewitness said no lifeguards were on duty. Someone finally ran up the beach to a man with a paddle board, she said, who went out to the two men. Both were pulled out of the water, although Mr. Surdyke was unresponsive. When they finally got Mr. Surdyke to shore, about five people began administering CPR.||Southampton Ambulance Chief Rick Fowler said a call came in at 3:58 p.m. for a swimmer in distress.  Twenty seven seconds later, a paramedic was in route to the scene, and arrived by 4:02 p.m.  The paramedic who arrived first, began using a defibrillator on the patient within 6 minutes of the call.  Twenty three minutes after taking over CPR, the patient was on his way to the Southampton Hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A moderate to high rip current risk affected the east-central Florida coast over the Memorial Day weekend, in part due to long period swells associated with Tropical Storm Bonnie which passed far offshore. Three swimmers were caught in rip currents, two in Brevard County on May 29 and the other on May 30 in Volusia County. Two of the swimmers died shortly after the incidents and the third passed away in a hospital approximately two weeks later.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: At about 1530LST on May 29, lifeguards at Spessard Holland Beach in Melbourne Beach rescued a 53 year old man from a rip current and resuscitated him. The man was transported to a local hospital, where he died approximately two weeks later. The cause of death was drowning. At about the same time of the initial incident, another lifeguard rescued two swimmers caught in a nearby rip current and noticed a third person submerged. The body of the third victim, a 20 year old male from Kissimmee, was recovered a few hours later. An autopsy confirmed he died due to drowning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A moderate to high rip current risk affected the east-central Florida coast over the Memorial Day weekend, in part due to long period swells associated with Tropical Storm Bonnie which passed far offshore. Three swimmers were caught in rip currents, two in Brevard County on May 29 and the other on May 30 in Volusia County. Two of the swimmers died shortly after the incidents and the third passed away in a hospital approximately two weeks later.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 62 year old man from North Carolina was caught in a rip current in Daytona Beach around 1000LST on May 30 and rescued by lifeguards, but became unconscious while being brought back to shore. Initial indications point to a stress-induced heart attack. He was taken to the hospital and pronounced dead. Since the exertion of fighting the rip current likely contributed to the heart attack, this death was recorded as a rip current fatality.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Elevated winds and seas along with shallow coastal flooding helped produce a period of rip currents along the Southeast South Carolina coast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Isle of Palms Fire and Rescue reported the rescue of an individual caught in a rip current between 41st and 42nd Avenue. Bystanders with boogie boards were able to assist in the rescue.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Elevated winds and seas along with shallow coastal flooding helped produce a period of rip currents along the Southeast South Carolina coast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Isle of Palms Fire and Rescue reported that they assisted in the rescue on an individual caught in a rip current between 41st and 42nd Avenue.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Elevated winds and seas along with shallow coastal flooding helped produce a period of rip currents along the Southeast South Carolina coast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Lifeguards from Folly Beach County Park assisted in the rescue of an individual caught in a rip current near the Folly Beach Pier.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A man was caught in a rip current and drowned. Still awaiting medical examination info.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man drowned after getting caught in a rip current.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two people drowned due to a rip current in Rodanthe.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 70 year old male was caught in a rip current and three men tried to rescue him. A 51 year old male was one of the men attempting rescue, and drowned in the rip current as well.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Long period swells with periods 14-16 seconds and swells of 2-3 ft were reported. These seas combined with breezy onshore flow created a High Risk of Rip currents along the local coast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A few rip current rescues occurred at Jacksonville Beach. A 4 ft surf with strong north to south longshore currents were reported with choppy water conditions.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A moderate risk of rip currents was in effect.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two children were caught in a rip current and rescued by lifeguards. Both were uninjured.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two teenagers were swimming in the ocean near Seaside and swept out to sea.  Both were rescued, but one died at the hospital.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two teenagers were swimming in the ocean near Seaside, OR. Lifeguards saw them struggling in the water in front of the turnaround.  Both were rescued and taken to the hospital, but one of the teens died at the hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A 64 year old woman drowned due to a rip current on Ocracoke Island.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 64 year old woman drowned due to a rip current on Ocracoke Island.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Moderate to strong east winds caused by high pressure over the western Atlantic and low pressure off the north coast of Cuba led to rip currents at the Atlantic beaches of South Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An unidentified man in his 30s was rescued by a good Samaritan from a rip current in Delray Beach. The man was unconscious when brought to shore and Ocean Rescue lifeguards were able to restore his breathing. The man was taken to the hospital where he was in stable condition upon arrival. Time is estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Rip currents were vigorous during the first half of August. Rescues were numerous including 60 people near Atlantic city on the 3rd and 4th. rescues for the 2nd and 3rd occurred at Harvey Ceders and Sea Girt. Several rescues occurred at North Wildwood on the 5th and nine additional rescues occurred from the 8th to the 10th. The 12th and 14th were active days in Cape May where 12 and 14 people were rescued respectively. Sadly, one person died sometime after being in a rip current while two others were sent to the hospital in North Wildwood on the 9th. Four additional rescues occurred on the 10th. Additional rescues occurred on the 21st at Sea Girt.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two people were injured while caught in a rip current. One person died after returning to shore.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A person got caught in a rip current and was injured from a breaking wave at Ocean City.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A person was rescued from a rip current but sustained an injury from a breaking wave.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A man visiting from California drowned near beach marker 228. He was last seen struggling between the second and third sandbar near the pier. The deceased was found the following morning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man visiting from California drowned in a rip current near the pier.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Energetic 3 to 4 foot swells from Tropical Cyclone Gaston brought rough surf and a high threat for rip current development to ocean beaches during the early to middle period of the week of August 28th. These dangerous conditions were highlighted in our Hazardous Weather Outlook starting early Saturday August 27th, with a Rip Current Statement being issued early Monday August 29th.  Unfortunately, one Brooklyn man drowned and another was rescued while swimming at Long Beach on the evening of Monday, August 29 after the lifeguards had left.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: One Brooklyn man drowned and another was rescued while swimming at Long Beach on the evening of Monday, August 29th. The men had been swimming in the ocean without a lifeguard on duty, when an emergency call came in at 6:26 p.m. Lifeguards and first responders performed CPR on one man while the other was rushed to the hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A teenage boy drowned in the water of Lake Superior in the Apostle Islands National Lakeshore after being pulled into deeper water by a rip current.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Strong currents pulled a swimmer into deep water off Stockton Island at Julian Bay, about 15 miles northeast of Bayfield. The victim was found after a 5 hour search. Sea conditions were rough with 8 foot waves and heavy, breaking surf on the beach.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong east winds brought rough seas and rip currents to all Atlantic beaches during the day. A man drowned near Miami Beach while rescuing another person caught in a rip current.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Several people were caught and rescued in a rip current that occurred near 23rd Street in Miami Beach. A 34-year-old man from Fort Myers went into the water to rescue his wife. The woman was able to escape, but the man was pulled from the water not breathing shortly thereafter. He later died at Mount Sinai Hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An extended period of onshore flow created persistent and dangerous rip currents along the coast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A total of 8 people were rescued by Jacksonville Beach lifeguards with 3 of the rescues transported to a local hospital due to injury.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Several rescues occurred on the 27th from rip currents. However one person suffered a spinal injury due getting caught in a rip current.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: One person suffered a spinal injury due to getting caught in a rip current.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A man went into the Gulf to try and rescue two swimmers in distress around 130 pm CDT on August 10th and did not return to shore.  Beach Police and surf patrol responded shortly afterwards to a call of swimmers in distress and were able to rescue the initial two swimmers, who were transported to the hospital for observation.  On Thursday afternoon, search and rescue located the body of the man offshore by helicopter.  A high rip current risk statement was in effect and had been in effect since August 5th.  Double red beach flags were also posted.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A young boy ventured out into the water around 200 yards from shore at Mustang Island State Park. Strong rip currents were reported to have pulled the male under water. Two other brothers had a difficult time making it back to shore. The deceased's body was later found a half mile away near Fish Pass. Local officials and US Coast Guard assisted in the search and rescue.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Strong rip currents pulled a young boy under water at Mustang Island State Park on the afternoon of the 16th. Two other brothers had a difficult time making it back to shore. The deceased's body was later found a half mile away near Fish Pass. Local officials and US Coast Guard assisted in the search and rescue.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Long period swells from Hurricane Nicole led to increased threat for rip currents and dangerous shore break. From the Outer Banks Sentinel newspaper, The body of a 17-year-old who died in rip currents on Oct. 13 was found Sunday evening, Oct. 16. According to the National Park Service, a visitor reported finding the body of the missing 17-year-old about 20 yards north of Avon Pier. He had been swimming with a 16-year-old friend when they were pulled into the ocean off the Cape Hatteras National Seashore beach in Waves. The 16-year-old was able to safely return to the beach and was taken to a hospital by ambulance.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 17 yr old male drowned in a rip current in Avon, NC. The victim was vacationing from Indiana.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Hazardous marine conditions affected the north coast of Puerto Rico producing dangerous rip current along the north facing beaches of Puerto Rico.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 33 year old man drowned due to rip currents at Balneario de Carolina beach.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Individual was swimming in the Gulf of Mexico on South Padre Island, during a day with a moderate risk of rip currents and rough surf. A 22 year old male went missing while swimming near the Bridgeport Condominiums near the 300 block of Padre Boulevard. His body was recovered on October 11.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 22 year old male swimming in the Gulf of Mexico on South Padre Island, near the 300 block of Padre Boulevard drowned in a rip current. His body was recovered on October 11 farther down the beach.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A 67 year old male drowned due to a rip current on Ocracoke Island.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 67 year old male drowned due to a rip current on Ocracoke Island.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A 71 year old male drowned due to a rip current in Frisco.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 71 year old male drowned due to a rip current in Frisco.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Multiple rescues at Myrtle Beach were a result of rip currents.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: There were 15 rip related rescues at Myrtle Beach.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong rip currents produced numerous rescues at Carolina Beach.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Ocean rescue reported 20 rip related rescues at Carolina Beach.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Light onshore flow and a passing upper level low south of the area brought lower than normal rain chances across the area. There was a low risk of rip currents.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 45 year old female died while trying to save her 11 year old son at the north end of Huguenot Park about a quarter mile from Ft. George Inlet. The drowning was attributed to both tidal currents and rip currents. Huguenot Park Beach has stronger ocean currents compared to other nearby beaches per Beach Patrol and Duval County EM. The park is on an island where Ft. George Inland borders to the north and the Mayport jetties border to the south. Changes also occurred to bathymetry in the area with sand bars and steeper drop offs into the ocean.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A 55 year old male from Virginia got caught in a rip current and drowned in Salvo around 10:06 AM on Sunday October 2, before going missing. His body was found and recovered on Tuesday October 4 around 7:36 AM.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 55 year old male from Virginia got caught in a rip current and drowned in Salvo around 10:06 AM on Sunday October 2, before going missing. His body was found and recovered on Tuesday October 4 around 7:36 AM.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Hazardous marine conditions due to northerly swells affecting the north coast of Puerto Rico. Dangerous Rip current were observed along the north facing beaches of Puerto Rico.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 14 year old boy drowned in a Rip current at Ocean Park beach in San Juan.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Moderate onshore winds led to rip currents at the Atlantic beaches of South Florida.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two rabbis visiting from New York drowned after being swept by rip currents at an unguarded beach near Haulover Inlet at 110th Street. A group of three men entered the water and began to struggle due to rip currents. One of the men made it back to shore and was hospitalized, while the other two drowned.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A female tourist was found floating face-down in the surf at Melbourne Beach after entering the ocean to swim. She was transported to a local hospital where she was pronounced brain dead, and died several days later. Strong rip currents were present on the day of the incident and two friends who were in the surf with her reported that they became caught in a rip current.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 52-year old woman from the State of Georgia was found floating face-down in the surf around 1500LST on January 15. She was transported to a local hospital by paramedics, was pronounced brain dead and died on January 18. Ocean Rescue reported rip currents in the area and two friends that the woman was swimming with reported that they became caught in a rip current. This rip current fatality becomes the first within east-central Florida during the month of January since records began in 1987.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A man died in Long Branch after getting caught by a rip current.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man got caught in a rip current and died.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Dangerous marine conditions produced rip currents across the northwest through northeast coastal areas of Puerto Rico.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 39 year old man from the state of Florida drowned at a beach in the municipality of Rincon.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Seas between 6 to 8 feet produced dangerous marine conditions along the north coast of Puerto Rico. Dangerous Rip current occurred along the north facing beaches of Puerto Rico.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 29 year old women from Guaynabo municipality drowned at Poza Las Mujeres in Manati. Reports indicated she was dragged by Rip Currents.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A 37 man died on the reef just off of Talafofo, Guam. The person died while fishing near the end of the month.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 37-year-old man died on the reef just off of Ipan Talofofo, Guam.||Guam Fire Department responded to a beach along the east side of Guam after 23:40 on the night of the 30th. At that time fire department personnel pulled a distressed fisherman to safety. ||The fisherman told the firefighters that he and a few other people were walking the reef, searching for lobsters. Since the other men could not be seen, searchers combed the Calvo Beach area near Ipan, Talofofo.||Sea heights just off-shore were between 8 and 9 feet as recorded by the Ipan wave rider buoy. The tide was also decreasing during the evening which may have helped enhance already strong currents. ||At around 10:00 am on the 31st, a U. S. Coast Guard boat recovered the body of the 37-year-old man outside the reef in front of the Calvo Beach in Ipan, Talofofo Guam.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Gusty southerly wind along with 2 to 3 foot seas led to rip currents in Palm Beach. One of these rip currents caused 4 people to be taken to a local hospital after being rescued by lifeguards.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Media reported a group of county lifeguards rescued four people in distress caught in a rip current. Two people were originally caught in the rip current when two others became caught while trying to assist them. All four swimmers were taken to nearby hospitals to recover.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong rip currents required multiple rescues at Carolina Beach.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An estimated 10 rescues were required due to rip currents. Reported by Ocean Rescue.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: There was a rip current fatality off the Galveston Island beach.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 20 year old male drowned near 63rd Street and Seawall Blvd.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong east wind and a incoming swell brought an elevated risk of rip currents to Atlantic coast beaches. A man drowned caught in a rip current at Palm Beach. Two others were injured and taken to the hospital trying to help.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A rip current at the 100 block of South Ocean Boulevard in Palm Beach killed one person and injured two others. A man was in distress caught in a rip current when another man attempted to rescue him. A police officer arrived and was able to pull both men out of the water. One man was unresponsive and was pronounced dead. The other man and the police officer were taken to local hospital and later released. The beach was unguarded at the time.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A 35 year old man visiting Padre Island drowned on the afternoon of the 28th. Emergency crews were sent to Beach Marker 230 near Bob Hall Pier. The man was transported to Bay Area Hospital in Corpus Christi where he was pronounced dead.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 35 year old man visiting Padre Island drowned in a rip current on the afternoon of the 28th. Emergency crews were sent to Beach Marker 230 near Bob Hall Pier. The man was pronounced dead at Bay Area Hospital in Corpus Christi.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Hazardous marine conditions affected the north coast of Puerto Rico. Dangerous rip current occurred along the north facing beaches of Puerto Rico.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: One Boy and one girl were swept away by Rip Currents in Montones beach at Barrio Bajuras. They were rescued.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Choppy surf and strong rip currents affected two children, resulting in one injury and a fatality.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An 8-year-old boy was caught in a strong rip current and pulled seaward at New Smyrna Beach. His 11-year-old sister attempted to rescue him and was also caught in the rip current. A bystander rescue the girl and returned her to shore, where she was transported to a hospital to treat her injuries. The body of the boy was recovered about a mile away on April 20. The fatality was a result of drowning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A moderate surf produced a rip current strong enough to cause a drowning in Galveston.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Moderate surf created a rip current strong enough to cause a drowning around 20 to 30 yards offshore near 35th street.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A teenage boy was swimming at the beach with friends when he was swept seaward in a strong rip current and drowned.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 16-year-old boy from Port St. Lucie drowned after being pulled seaward by a strong rip current and disappeared from view. A sheriffs office helicopter and water and boat patrol crews found the boy and returned him to shore. Rescuers performed CPR and then transported him to a local hospital where he was pronounced dead a short time later. The death was a result of drowning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong rip currents resulted in over three dozen rescues by life guards along the Volusia County coastline throughout the day. Another man was found unconscious in the water and was pulled to shore by first responders.

Hundreds of piers were damaged or destroyed n Mobile and Baldwin Counties. Some coastal roads were also closed due to surge, including the US Highway 90 Causeway and Water Street in Downtown Mobile. The surge and large breaking waves also resulted in significant beach erosion along the gulf facing beaches. 6 feet of sand was deposited on a 3 mile stretch of Bienville Blvd on the west end of Dauphin Island. ||Winds gusts of 50+ mph were observed in coastal areas with a the highest wind gust of 66 mph recorded at the Mobile Regional Airport just after 2am on October 8th. EVENT_NARRATIVE: Ozaukee County Emergency Manager first alerted WFO MKX about a missing swimmer at Harrington Beach State Park along the Lake Michigan shore.  A group of 5 people went swimming in dangerous swimming conditions when strong onshore winds were creating high waves and an increased risk of sub-surface currents.  Of the five swimmers, four people returned to the beach.  Of the four, a woman in her 30s suffered life-threatening injures due to water inhalation, and died.  The missing male swimmer turned up about two weeks later on September 4th at Whitefish Dunes State Park, about 120 miles north along the Lake Michigan shore.  An autopsy confirmed the male died from drowning.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A prolonged and oppressive heat wave swept the Central Coast and Bay Area for almost a week from August 14th to August 19th with widespread record breaking temperatures observed across the region. This was caused by a strong high pressure system over the Desert Southwest that expanded westward into California. This dome of heat brought hot temperatures to the area for several days. Multiple days of triple digit afternoon highs were recorded inland with some coastal locations even reaching the mid 90s. Several days of hot and dry weather further dried fuels over the area increasing fire danger. During this event, a surge of monsoonal and tropical moisture from a former Tropical Storm advected northward with sufficient instability to generate multiple high based and dry thunderstorms that produced several thousand lightning strikes over the Greater Bay Area. Many locations saw wind gusts of 40-50 mph with isolated areas seeing gusts of 60-75 mph. This prompted the San Francisco Bay Area forecast office to issue a rare severe thunderstorm warning. These lightning strikes in combination with gusty and erratic outflow winds sparked hundreds of wildfires across the state of California. Several smaller fires combined to form complexes some of which are now among the largest wildfires in state history. Most of which were still actively burning at the end of August. Hundreds of thousands of acres have been burned with several hundred structures destroyed as well as a handful of deaths and injuries. Tens of thousands of residents were also forced to evacuate. Additionally, all of these wildfires burning simultaneously across the state gave the Bay Area the worst air quality in the world at one point.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Dry gusty offshore winds as well as strengthening high pressure enabled the generation and rapid spread of the Glass Fire across Napa and Sonoma counties at the end of September. The mountains of the North Bay saw wind gusts of 40 to 65 mph into the morning of the 28th with 30 to 40 mph gusts across the East Bay Hills. These gusty winds along with dry conditions enabled the Glass Fire to spread almost fourfold in one day. Tens of thousands of residents were evacuated and nearly 80 homes were destroyed along with numerous additional structures including a famous Napa winery. Offshore flow and strong high pressure also broke several daily temperature records across the SF Bay Area. High temperatures were in the mid/upper 90s to low 100s inland and mid 80s to low 90s along the coast.

Once the ridge began to break down towards the end of the weekend, offshore winds increased flaring up some of the wildfires that were ignited during August's lightning storm. EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A dangerous rip current event unfolded along the mid-Atlantic coast on September 18. Tropical Storm Odette was moving further out to sea as it began to transition to an extratropical cyclone. However, swells associated with the storm continued to impact the coast with high seas and dangerous rip currents. Combined with most beaches no longer being guarded due to the time of year, but with warm and mostly sunny weather conditions present, a number of swimmers came into distress along the New Jersey coastline. First responders rescued over a dozen swimmers from the surf over the course of the day, and sadly one fatality occurred in Ocean County, New Jersey.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 54 year old man was pulled from the surf around 12:30 local time and was pronounced dead soon after at a local hospital. Over a dozen other swimmers were rescued in Ocean County alone.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 17 year old girl died from drowning on November 25th. She was swimming with her a group of her friends near Gregorio Perez Park in Mangilao on the afternoon of November 25th. Here sister said they were out 50 feet form the shore, and all of them started to go under the water and drown. She was holding on to one of her friends when she realized she might be endangering both of them. She let go of her friend, who made it to shore, but unfortunately floundered in the swell and drowned. It took about an hour for rescuers to find her body. Ritidian buoy showed the largest waves between 8 and 9 feet with a 10 second period. A long period north swell was producing a high risk of rip currents.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Long period swells generated a rip currents over the Marianas in November.  Two events occurred at Guam during the month.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: At 12:39 p.m. the Guam Fire Department responded to reports of a distressed swimmer near Jeff's Pirates Cove, in Talo'fo'fo'. After arriving onsite, the Fire Department learned that the individual was rescued by others on shore and an employee of Jeff's Pirates Cove. The employee used a jet ski to rescue the individual. Further explaining by Jeff's Pirates Cove owner explained that after one person became caught in a rip current, two others tried to help him, but likewise became caught in the current. The restaurant employee on the jet ski rescued all three people. A long period east swell east swell was generating a high rip current risk.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Very strong rip currents at local beaches on the afternoon of October 12th contributed to a drowning on South Padre Island.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 17-year old man drowned in a rip current at approximately 4 PM CDT on Wednesday, October 12th, in the surf at Cameron County Public Access #5. The teen was with a group of peers but entered the surf on his own and, according to the witnesses, disappeared into the waves. According to USCG, witnesses reported the swimmer began demonstrating signs of distress, and the currents soon overpowered him before he submerged. A 9-1-1 call from the peer group was related to USCG Corpus Christi, where air assets were deployed, along with water assets from USCG South Padre Island to assist with SAR. Cameron County Beach Patrol, Cameron County Emergency Management, and South Padre island Fire Department assisted in the SAR. The swimmer was recovered a day later (October 13), 8 miles north of the entry point, by Cameron Co. Park Rangers after fishers discovered the floating body and called 9-1-1.

The swimmers were two juvenile females that stated that they were swept out into the lake while swimming in waist to chest deep water. Her friend came into the water to save her and was also caught in the rip current. Upon arrival, Duluth Fire learned that the swimmers were rescued by a passerby. The rescuer was walking the beach with a companion and said that he heard the cry for help. He reported that one of the swimmers had mostly made it to shore. He quickly went for the second swimmer. Both of the swimmers were safely retrieved and examined by paramedics, but did not require medical care.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A rip current at Martin's Beach in Half Moon Bay swept four people out to sea on Saturday November 25. The four had gotten too close to the water, lost their footing, and went into the water. Two of the people self-rescued, the other two, a 5-year-old girl and her grandfather (a 54-year-old man), were swept out to sea. The timing of the event is unclear, but the Coast Guard search started at 1:20 PM. The girl was recovered and taken to the hospital, where she was pronounced dead. The man remains missing, and the search was called off the next day. At the time of the incident, the SF Bar buoy (46237) reported wave heights of 7 to 8 feet at 18 to 20 seconds. Winds were offshore (out of the E/NE) generally around 10 mph near the Half Moon Bay coastline.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Breaking waves around 3 to 5 feet, multiple swell groups from offshore Hurricane Franklin and Idalia, and a dominant long period onshore swell resulted in dangerous rip currents at the New Jersey shore. A HIGH risk for rip currents was in effect.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast media reports that three people in Beach Haven were caught in a rip current during the afternoon of September 3rd. Two were rescued, but one person was pronounced dead.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Breaking waves around 3 to 5 feet, multiple swell groups from offshore Hurricane Franklin and Idalia, and a dominant long period onshore swell resulted in dangerous rip currents at the New Jersey shore. A HIGH risk for rip currents was in effect.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast media reports multiple swimmers in Seaside Park had to be rescued after being caught in a rip current. 1 swimmer was pronounced dead.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Breaking waves around 3 to 5 feet, multiple swell groups from offshore Hurricane Franklin and Idalia, and a dominant long period onshore swell resulted in dangerous rip currents at the New Jersey shore. A HIGH risk for rip currents was in effect.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast media reports multiple swimmers were caught in a rip current during the evening of September 3rd and had to be rescued. One swimmer was pronounced dead with a few others being transported to the hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The tropical cyclones centered well north of the islands, into the open Atlantic waters, continued to generate swells that deteriorated marine and coastal conditions along the northern coast of Puerto Rico. At least two lives were lost due to strong rip currents.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Emergency managers and broadcast media reported a 31-year-old female that was found drowned near La Pocita in Loiza. The victim was likely swept away by rip currents.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A northerly s well from Hurricane Lee deteriorated marine and coastal conditions along the area. Breaking waves just shy from 14 feet were observed along many areas in northern Puerto Rico. The breaking waves managed to bring sand into vulnerable roads.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 66-year-old male drowned in Poza del Obispo, near road PR-681 in Arecibo.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The tropical cyclones centered well north of the islands, into the open Atlantic waters, continued to generate swells that deteriorated marine and coastal conditions along the northern coast of Puerto Rico. At least two lives were lost due to strong rip currents.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 15-year-old male was swept away by rip currents at a beach near Los Kioskos de Luquillo. The victim was recovered on 09/18/2023 around 1:15 PM AST.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A male in his 60s from Kansas died on Sunday at the 1000 block of West Beach Blvd near 10th St in Gulf Shores, AL. The male was at an unguarded beach when he was swept away from the beach by a rip current. Bystanders were able to get the male out of the water, but once lifeguards and firefighters got to him, they could not resuscitate him. Single red flags were flying in Gulf Shores. There were at least a dozen rescues for distressed swimmers in the last two weeks, and this was the first drowning of the year in Gulf Shores. Pensacola Beach and Orange Beach also reported several rip current rescues on Sunday. The weather was very nice on Sunday with highs in the 80s.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A male in his 60s from Kansas died on Sunday at the 1000 block of West Beach Blvd near 10th St in Gulf Shores, AL. The male was at an unguarded beach when he was swept away from the beach by a rip current. Bystanders were able to get the male out of the water, but once lifeguards and firefighters got to him, they could not resuscitate him. Single red flags were flying in Gulf Shores. There were at least a dozen rescues for distressed swimmers in the last two weeks and this was the first drowning of the year in Gulf Shores. Pensacola Beach and Orange Beach also reported several rip current rescues on Sunday. The weather was very nice on Sunday with highs in the 80s.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Onshore NNE winds and elevated high astronomical tides created an elevated rip current risk at local beaches. A moderate rip current risk of rip currents was advertised.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Five people were rescued at North 11th Street and A1A along in Flagler Beach. A separate rescue of 1 person occurred near the Flagler Beach pier. There were no sustained injuries reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A high rip current risk was in effect for all SE GA and NE FL beaches due to long wave periods up to 15 seconds originating from distant Tropical Cyclone Lee over the Atlantic.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The body of a missing 14-year-old male was recovered on 9/14 after being overtaken by a rip current on 9/13. An adult and another teenager were also caught in the rip current, but they were rescued and transported to a local hospital in stable condition.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A coastal low tracked north of the region. A couple days of strong onshore flow and elevated tides with swells from the low created a High Rip Current risk.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 19 year old male went missing in the evening around 7:30 pm local time in the ocean at Jacksonville Beach. His body was recovered on Wednesday 5/31. Ocean lifeguards likely contributed to the drowning. Big sandbars and sloughs were reported as well. There was a high rip current risk in effect. Surf was expected to be 4-6 ft per the surf zone forecast.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved through on July 29th 2023 kicking waves up to around 3 feet during the afternoon. Winds relaxed to around 1 foot at the time of the incident, but lingering currents were present. Witnesses stated the father and son were struggling to fight the currents, which were likely a combination of rip and longshore currents as winds were northeast during the event. The son was rescued by a nearby jet skier, but the father was unable to hold on and later drowned.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A cold front moved through on July 29th 2023 kicking waves up to around 3 feet during the afternoon. Winds relaxed to around 1 foot at the time of the incident, but lingering currents were still present. Witnesses stated the father and son were struggling to fight the currents, which were likely a combination of rip and longshore currents as winds were northeast during the event. The son was rescued by a nearby jet skier, but the father was unable to hold on and later drowned.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Hazardous coastal conditions where observed across the northern coastline from Rincon to Fajardo due to long-dominant period northwesterly to northerly swell and vigorous to fresh winds impacting the regional waters. High Surf Advisories and a High Risk of Rip Currents were in effect for Fajardo, where four people were swept away by strong rip currents at Playa Escondida (one fatality and three injured).
EVENT_NARRATIVE: On December 9th, Emergency Managers in Fajardo, PR, reported that four people were swept away by strong rip currents at Playa Escondida, Fajardo. Emergency Managers successfully rescued three out of the four individuals, but unfortunately, a young 25-year-old adult from San Lorenzo, Puerto Rico, drowned. The body was found about 1,500 ft from the coastline on December 11th.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The combination of strong winds and increased swell led to increased rip currents along Gulf Coast beaches. On June 22nd, a 47 year old man from Georgia died after rescuing his son at Gulf State Park. On June 23rd, a man died trying to rescue his son from a rip current. The son made it to safety.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 47 year old male from Georgia died near the Gulf State Park Pavilion in Gulf Shores trying to save his son.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The combination of strong winds and increased swell led to increased rip currents along Gulf Coast beaches. On June 22nd, a 47 year old man from Georgia died after rescuing his son at Gulf State Park. On June 23rd, a man died trying to rescue his son from a rip current. The son made it to safety.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man died along Fort Morgan. He was trying to rescue his son. The age and hometown are not known.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A father and son were pulled from the ocean near Pacifica on January 14. At 12:52 PM, two fire companies, a rescue unit, a CHP helicopter, state park personnel and Coast Guard air and water units responded to the two people struggling in the water north of Mori Point. Rescue swimmers pulled the two people from the water and took them to ambulances, which transported them to San Francisco General Hospital. At the time of the rescue, the San Francisco buoy (46026) reported waves of 2.7 meters (9 feet) at 15 seconds, with a water temperature of 12.5 degrees Celsius (54.5 degrees Fahrenheit).
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A father and son were pulled from the ocean near Pacifica on January 14. At 12:52 PM, two fire companies, a rescue unit, a CHP helicopter, state park personnel and Coast Guard air and water units responded to the two people struggling in the water north of Mori Point. Rescue swimmers pulled the two people from the water and took them to ambulances, which transported them to San Francisco General Hospital.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure over the Atlantic Ocean brought moderate onshore winds to the coast of Broward County in South Florida, which led to strong rip currents and rough surf.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Fort Lauderdale Fire Rescue reported that responders rescued 6 distressed swimmers. One was transported to a hospital. Moderate onshore winds led to a high risk of rip currents along the beaches of Broward County. Time is estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure over the Atlantic Ocean brought moderate onshore winds to the coast of Broward County in South Florida, which led to strong rip currents and rough surf.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Fort Lauderdale Fire Rescue reported that responders rescued two distressed swimmers. Moderate onshore winds led to a high risk of rip currents along the beaches of Broward County. Time is estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Locally generated rip currents on a low-risk day caused a drowning in Isabela.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A tourist drowned on Jobos Beach.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A low-pressure system located approximately 900 miles north of Puerto Rico generated significant northerly swells during the week of March 27th. These swells caused high surf and life-threatening rip currents along the Atlantic coastline of the islands.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 40-year-old male tourist and his two daughters were swept away by rip currents at Montones Beach in Isabela. The man managed to rescue the girls but was also dragged and unable to get out of the water. Paramedics from State Medical Emergencies provided first aid and confirmed that the individual no longer had vital signs.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Wind-driven seas and a fading long-period northeasterly swell caused a high risk of rip currents along Puerto Rico's Atlantic Coastline.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A family of seven was swept away by rip currents in Playa Escondida, Fajardo. The father was able to save all his children and wife, but he drowned, and his body was recovered two days later in the area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Seas were slowly building across the Atlantic waters on Sunday, March 10th, from swells generated by a distant surface low. Although this would lead to a high risk of rip currents on Monday, a moderate risk prevailed through Sunday.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two males were swept away by rip currents near Ventana del Mar, behind La Concha Hotel in Condado. According to initial reports, a local resident tried to rescue a tourist who had been pulled away by the currents. They both drowned. The first victim was identified as a 20-year-old male from Washington visiting the island for Spring Break. The second victim was a staff sergeant in the Puerto Rico Army National Guard, his body was recovered three miles from the beach two days later on March 12.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Large northerly swells affected the Atlantic coastline of Puerto Rico during the week of March 13th. This produced large breaking waves higher than 10 feet and life-threatening rip currents along the north and east-facing beaches of the islands.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A rip current swept away a 52-year-old male tourist from Minnesota at La Pared Beach in Luquillo on March 13th. The person was rescued and taken to the Caribbean Medical Center in critical condition, where he died.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A low-pressure system located approximately 900 miles north of Puerto Rico generated significant northerly swells during the week of March 27th. These swells caused high surf and life-threatening rip currents along the Atlantic coastline of the islands.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A rescue operation began on March 28 for a 26-year-old tourist, an active duty U.S. marine, and a resident of Massachusetts who was swept away by rip currents on La Pared beach in Luquillo on March 27. The Coast Guard rescue crews suspended search efforts on April 1 in support of local emergency response agencies. He is presumed dead.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Residual 4 to 5 ft swells from the passage of Tropical Depression Debby well to the north and west of the region on Friday August 9th, resulted in a moderate to high risk for rip current development along eastern Long Island ocean beaches. A likely rip current fatality occurred in these conditions on August 11th along the outer beaches of Smith Point Park.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: On August 11th at about noon, a Suffolk County Park Ranger who was patrolling Smith Point was on the outer beach between cut 1 and cut 2 was was notified that a person was in distress in the water. Fire Rescue officials were also notified and activated the Mastic Beach FD, along with the local Marine Incident Response Team (MIRT), which in addition to Mastic Beach FD also consists of Mastic Fire Department, Eastport FD, Center Moriches FD, and East Moriches FD. Also activated were the Mastic and Mastic Beach Ambulance Companies. ||The Mastic FD Marine Incident Response Boat 5-12-26 was already out conducting overwatch for the Suffolk County USAR team that was conducting a drill on the Forge river when the call went out. With a full crew and an EMT on board, they broke off from the drill immediately once the call went out for persons in the water on the ocean side at Smith Point.||Mastic Beach FD, under command of Chief Luis Grego and Assistant Chief Jason Sharp, also sent members to the dock to meet the boat. The remaining members of the MIRT team also began to quickly muster crews and resources for response. Suffolk Police Marine Rescue Boat Marine Mike was also dispatched. While units were responding from Police and Fire Departments, the Park Ranger and a good Samaritan had attempted to send out a life ring, but the man was unresponsive. ||Suffolk County Ocean Rescue lifeguards responded to the location, which is outside of the protected zone of jet skis and located the unresponsive 70-year-old male. He was taken to shore where CPR was initiated. Smith Point EMTs were on scene and assisted with care, which was turned over to members of the Mastic Beach Ambulance.||Park Rangers met with Suffolk Police at the outer beach entrance where police requested that the road to the outer beach be closed at the booth. Mastic Beach Ambulance transported the male to Long Island Community Hospital where he was later pronounced dead.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Large north swell generated by a distant extratropical cyclone, along with elevated wind waves and northeast swell from a descending shear line into the Marianas, created dangerous surf and rip currents along west and north facing reefs of the Marianas from January 17-19, with surf then slowly decreasing through January 22.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Firefighters were called to a beach near the village of Asan (across from the old Harley-Davidson store) for a report of two swimmers in distress at 1424ChST. A 13-year-old boy was found and pulled onto the boat, and he did not require any medical attention. the 8-year-old was later found and CPR administered as he was transported to Naval Hospital. It was later reported that the 8-year-old boy later passed away at the hospital. This occurred at the tail end of large surf event created by large north swell and a shear line that brought choppy seas due to strong winds, that started January 17th.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A 17 year old boy from Minnesota went missing on the afternoon of the 6th while swimming in Lake Michigan near Beverly Shores. He was unable to be recovered. Three others were rescued from the water and transported to a local hospital. A Beach Hazards Statement was in effect at the time advertising 6 to 9 foot waves and dangerous currents along the Indiana lakeshore.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Two men required rescuing after jumping into the lake near 12th Street Beach on the afternoon of the 7th. Both men were recovered and transported to a local hospital in critical condition. One of the individuals later died in the hospital. A Beach Hazards Statement was in effect at the time advertising 4 to 7 foot waves and dangerous currents along the Illinois lakeshore.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A couple of water rescues were required at Illinois Lake Michigan beaches on the 18th. One 16 year old boy unfortunately succumbed to the dangerous swimming conditions.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 16 year old boy went missing in Lake Michigan at Rainbow Beach on the afternoon of the 18th. His body was recovered three days later. A Beach Hazards Statement was in effect at the time advertising 6 to 10 foot waves and dangerous currents along the Illinois lakeshore.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: There was a rip current fatality.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 26 year old male from Leesville, LA drowned in a rip current near 24th Street. In addition, lifeguards rescued at least a dozen other people throughout the day that were rip current/surf related.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A 40 year old male visitor drowned after he and his juvenile son were swept out into the Gulf of Mexico by a rip current. Both father and son were taken to the hospital. The son was reportedly in stable condition, but the father did not survive. The drowning occurred at James Lee Park in Destin.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 40 year old male visitor drowned after he and his juvenile son were swept out into the Gulf of Mexico by a rip current. Both father and son were taken to the hospital. The son was reportedly in stable condition, but the father did not survive. The drowning occurred at James Lee Park in Destin.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A mix of northerly and easterly swells led to hazardous conditions in the surf zone of Guam.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Guam Fire Department received a call at 1100ChST of distressed swimmers at Ritidian Beach. GFD Rescue, Coast Guard and the Navy's HSC-25 helicopter squadron were on scene to conduct search and rescue operations. When GFD arrived, they learned a 28-year-old man was last seen going over the reef, while two other men who were also with the first swimmer were able to make it back to shore. One of the two men who made it back to shore was transported to Guam Regional Medial City for evaluation, while the other refused any service. The body of the man who went over the reef, was found approximately 25 fee below the surface, at 0809ChST the following day. Ritidian Beach is known for its strong rip currents as the reef line is relatively close to shore and there are large cuts in the reef that favor rip currents.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A mix of northerly and easterly swells led to hazardous conditions in the surf zone of Guam.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: At 1328ChST, Guam Fire Department (GFD) received a report that a 40-year-old fisherman was overdue. He was fishing in the waters off Asan Beach. The search was called off Wednesday night, but was resumed 0600ChST Thursday morning. At 0752ChST Thursday morning, GFD divers located the fisherman's body at approximately 45 feet below the surface of the water. It is  believed the fisherman was wading in the water and got caught in a rip current that pulled in deeper into the water and towards the reef line.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A fading long-period northeasterly swell was maintaining hazardous surf conditions across the northern coast of Puerto Rico. Breaking waves were in the order of 10 to 11 feet for these beaches.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man was found floating on the waters near Playa Montones in Isabela. The individual was found dead.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong high pressure system centered well to the south of American Samoa created stronger than usual east/southeasterly trades winds throughout the American Samoa islands and along the territory's coastal waters. ASCAT readings showed 15 to 20 knot winds along the coastal waters. Due to the stronger winds than normal, along with a long fetch of elevated winds, this led to choppy and hazardous seas in the region. Altimeter data from POES satellites showed waves between 8 and 9 feet.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Local broadcast media reports that the Department of Search and Rescue began searching for a man who was swept out at sea due to rough seas while swimming along the coastline of Fogagogo village on the afternoon of April 2nd. Due to continuing rough sea conditions, the search operation was limited throughout the overnight hours on the 2nd and the morning of the 3rd, but resumed on the afternoon of the 3rd. The search continued through the 8th. The body was not found.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong rip currents developed at area beaches and resulted a death of man in his mid 70s in Destin. Another person died at Langdon Beach in the Gulf Islands National Seashore.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man in his mid 70s visiting from out of state was caught in a rip current. This occurred at 1006 East Highway 98 near Jade East Towers in Destin.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong rip currents developed at area beaches and resulted a death of man in his mid 70s in Destin. Another person died at Langdon Beach in the Gulf Islands National Seashore.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: One person drowned around 440pm. This occurred at Langdon Beach, inside the Ft. Pickens gate in the Gulf Islands National Seashore.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A Potential Tropical Cyclone became Tropical Storm Alberto as it moved generally westward across the southern Gulf of Mexico and made landfall in the Tampico area. Coastal flooding occurred along the upper Texas coast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 17-year-old from Louisiana drowned on west side of Tower 25 according to Beach Patrol.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Moderate Swim risk with 2-3ft waves and onshore winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 17 year old male was found dead last night after drowning in Lake Michigan off of Bender Park in Oak Creek, WI (Milwaukee Co). He was swimming with his family at Bender Park Beach when a rip current (Likely structural given photos near break wall) swept him and two other teenagers under the water. Another teenager was hospitalized. Moderate Swim Risk conditions with messaging in MKX HWO.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Persistent south to southwest winds brought 3 ft breaking surf and a moderate risk of rip currents to the local beaches on Friday. In addition, hot and humid conditions had large crowds flocking to area beaches. Two rip current fatalities occurred in these conditions after hours on 6/21 at Jacob Riis Park.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Shortly after 6 p.m. after lifeguards had left for the day, Christian Perkins, who had just turned 17 the week before, and 16-year-old Elyjha Chandler, went into the ocean near Bay 2 in Riis Park, to cool off during the heatwave. The boys did not know how to swim. Witnesses say the teens tried to jump up when a large wave came, but the wave consumed them, and they never resurfaced. By 6:35 p.m., 911 calls were made to report the missing boys. The call resulted in a massive rescue response that included FDNY Marine Units and divers, NYPD Harbor Units, NYPD Harbor Base Divers, and Coast Guard and water teams from Sandy Hook, Cape Cod and Atlantic City. They searched for the boys until darkness fell on Friday, with no sight of them. They resumed the search the next day, until the search was suspended on Saturday night. Coast Guard crews had searched a total of more than 600 square miles. The search area extended from Sandy Hook, New Jersey, to Long Beach, New York, and offshore approximately 20 nautical miles. ||Their bodies were found over a week later. Police said one of the bodies was found Saturday night June 29 around 9 p.m. near Beach 114th Street and Ocean Promenade in Queens. The other body was found Sunday June 30th around 10:45 a.m. near Beach 149th Street and Rockaway Beach Boulevard��� almost two miles west.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong swells from distant Hurricane Ernesto led to strong rip currents, multiple rescues, and one drowning in southeast North Carolina.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Wrightsville Beach Ocean Rescue performed 25 rip current rescues due to strong rip currents caused by Hurricane Ernesto.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strengthening southerly winds brought a moderate to high risk for rip current development along NYC ocean beaches with a combo of 3 to 4 foot southerly wind wave and 2 foot easterly swells. In addition, hot and humid conditions had large crowds flocking to area beaches. Two rip current fatalities occurred in these conditions after hours on July 5th at Coney Island Beach.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Aisha Mohammed, 18, and Zainab Mohammed, 17, of the Bronx were reported missing around 8:10 p.m. Friday near Stillwell Avenue in Brooklyn by a bystander who said they entered the water and disappeared from view. The teens were found on the shoreline at 9:15 p.m. and rushed to Coney Island Hospital, where they were pronounced dead according to the NYPD. ||A relative said it was only their second time going to the beach. They were hanging out with a group of about 12 other people enjoying a sunny day at the popular beach when the skies suddenly opened up in a heavy downpour. A family member said he was returning to the group when he spotted the girls being swept out to sea in a strong current.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A surface high pressure across the Atlantic and a tropical wave moving across the CWA promoted moderate to fresh east to southeasterly winds over the local area. This caused seas to increase between 4 and 5 feet across the southern coastal waters of Puerto Rico, and a moderate risk of rip currents was expected across the south to southeastern beaches of Puerto Rico. One drowning occurred in Guilarte Beach in Arroyo.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An 86-year-old male was found floating in Playa Guilarte in Arroyo, PR. A 911 call alerted the authorities and took the victim to a nearby hospital, where the doctors confirmed the fatality.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A flash rip current developed and led to a drowning in Myrtle Beach.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 15 year old teen drowned in a flash rip current in Myrtle Beach, SC around 12th Ave S.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong swells from distant Hurricane Ernesto led to strong rip currents, multiple rescues, and one drowning in southeast North Carolina.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 41 year old male drowned in a rip current in Surf City during the afternoon of the 17th attempting to rescue two children caught in a strong current caused by swells from Hurricane Ernesto.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: Prolonged period of strong rip currents and multiple rescues were reported by ocean rescue groups in New Hanover County. Between June 18th and 22nd, Carolina Beach reported 95 rip current rescues, Wrightsville Beach reported 24 rescues, and Kure Beach reported 45 rip current rescues.
