EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Four people required rescuing while swimming near Lighthouse Beach during the afternoon of the 30th. Three of the four swimmers, two teenage girls and one adult woman, were rescued. One of the teenagers was transported to a hospital where she was treated and released while the others did not require hospital treatment. The fourth swimmer, a 41 year old man, could not be recovered. Rescue efforts continued into the next day but officials called off the search that afternoon when they were still unable to locate the man. His body was found 5 days later on July 5th by a fishing charter roughly two miles offshore from Dempster Street Beach. At the time of the incident, a red no swimming flag was flying at the beach, no lifeguards were on duty, and a water closed, no swimming sign was sitting at the entrance of the beach. A beach hazards statement and small craft advisory were in effect at the time advertising waves up to 8 feet.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Breezy northeast winds between low pressure offshore and high pressure inland led to conditions favorable for rip currents along the Southeast South Carolina coast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A Colleton County emergency manager reported two individuals were rescued from|a strong rip current near 102 Palmetto Boulevard. An adult male was able to break free of the rip current and made it back to shore. An adult female was rescued after being found unconscious by emergency personnel entering the water. After being stabilized, she was flown to MUSC for emergency care.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Breezy east-northeast winds between low pressure developing across the Gulf Stream and weak high pressure inland led to conditions favorable for rip currents along the Southeast Georgia coast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Tybee Island lifeguards reported several small rip currents between 17th Street and 10th Street, leading to 5 rip current related rescues on Tybee Island.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High surf and strong rip currents along the beaches of east central Florida produced dangerous swimming conditions. A married couple visiting from Pennsylvania drowned in the waters near Stuart Beach.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 48-year-old female and 51-year-old male were pulled from the rough surf in an unguarded portion of Stuart Beach, FL near the intersection of SE Macarthur Blvd. and NE Tradewind Ln. Martin County Ocean Rescue Lifeguards performed CPR on the victims before the two were transported to Martin North Hospital where they later died. The mother and father of six were vacationing from Pennsylvania. Two of their teen children were also caught in the rip current; however, they were able break the current and swim back to shore.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An enhanced gradient wind between high pressure centered south of the region and low pressure passing to the north along with a developing sea breeze near the coast led to favorable conditions for rip currents along southeast South Carolina beaches.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Post and Courier reported two males 15 years old or younger caught in a rip current near Folly Beach Pier and being rescued by a member of the public.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The combination of onshore flow, sufficient swell energy, and lingering astronomical influences produced an enhanced rip current risk along the southeast South Carolina coast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Folly Beach lifeguards observed 1 moderate strength rip current near 2nd Street West. There was 1 rescue associated with this rip current.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure over the western Atlantic led to a steady easterly onshore wind flow across the Atlantic coast of South Florida, creating ideal conditions for rip current formation.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast media reported one fatality due to strong rip currents in Dania Beach near           North Beach Rd. Four people total had began to struggle due to the rip currents. A father drowned while trying to rescue his son. Two others were rescued by U.S. Coast Guard personnel, as well as two off-duty Hollywood lifeguards who assisted after-hours.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A 17 year old female drowned in a rip current at Ocean Isle Beach, NC.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 17 year old female drowned in a rip current shortly after noon at Ocean Isle Beach, NC. Two other teens who were caught in the rip current were rescued.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Persistent southeast swell and holiday crowd, along with forerunner swells from Hurricane Beryl arriving on the 4th, led to multiple days of strong rip currents and numerous rescues at New Hanover County beaches.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Prolonged period of strong rip currents and multiple rescues were reported by ocean rescue groups in New Hanover County. Between July 3rd and July 7th, Wrightsville Beach reported 99 rip current rescues, Carolina Beach reported 86 rescues, and Kure Beach reported 14 rip current rescues.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Strong rip currents led to a drowning at Kure Beach, NC around noon on July 4th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 21 year old male from Raleigh, NC got caught in a strong rip current before going missing at Kure Beach around noon and is presumed dead.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A 17 year old male drowned in a rip current at Litchfield Beach.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two teens were caught in a strong rip current at Litchfield Beach the evening of July 12th. One teen made it back to shore. The other teen, a 17 year old male, drowned.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A 14-year-old Toledo, OH boy drowned in Lake Superior on the 24th after being caught in a rip current at a beach near the Lake Superior State Forest Campground in Luce County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 14-year-old Toledo, OH boy drowned in Lake Superior on the 24th after being caught in a rip current at a beach near the Lake Superior State Forest Campground.  A 15-year-old was also caught in the rip current but was able to swim to the safety of shallow water.  The Coast Guard, Luce County Sheriff and Michigan DNR conservation officers conducted a search by boat and helicopter until dusk on the evening of the 24th , but waves of 4 to 5 feet at the time of the drowning hindered search and recovery efforts.  The search continued on the next day with additional aid from the Michigan State Police Dive and Drone Team until the victim's body was recovered that afternoon on the 25th.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An eleven-year-old boy drowned in a rip current at Conneaut Township Park Beach during the afternoon of the 7th. The incident occurred when northwesterly onshore winds were around 20 knots and waves were as large as 3 to 6 feet along the Ashtabula County shore. A Beach Hazards Statement was in effect for a high risk of rip currents along the southern lakeshore from Erie County, OH to Erie County, PA. The relatively-strong onshore surface winds were generated by a relatively-tight southwesterly MSLP gradient over Lake Erie, between a surface low centered over the Gulf of Maine and a surface high centered in vicinity of northeastern AR.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An eleven-year-old boy drowned in a rip current at Conneaut Township Park Beach during the afternoon of June 7th. Since the news article stated the victim was swept away while visiting the park Friday afternoon, the time of the incident is estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A 22 year old man went swimming in Lake Michigan early in the morning of July 1st and went missing.  He was found unresponsive in the water near Montrose Beach.  He was taken to a local hospital where he was pronounced dead.  Waves at the nearby Wilmette buoy were 3 to 5 feet.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A weak high pressure is ridding over the region from a high pressure just west of the Canary Islands maintained light and variable winds. This promoted seas of 3 to 4 feet, occasionally higher over the Atlantic waters of Puerto Rico. There was a moderate risk of rip currents in effect for the northern beaches of Puerto Rico, including Isabela. One rip current related drowning occurred in Jobos Beach.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A newspaper reported that a 59-year-old tourist was spending time with his 9-year-old son and 12-year-old daughter at Jobos Beach when they were swept away by rip currents. Two surfers at the beach rescued the children and then returned to retrieve the father, whom they brought to shore, but he had no vital signs upon arrival.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A surface high pressure across the Atlantic promoted gentle to moderate easterly winds. Seas were around 4 feet, occasionally to 5 feet, over the coastal northern waters of Puerto Rico. There was a moderate risk of rip currents in effect for the northern beaches of Puerto Rico, including San Juan. One rip current related drowning occurred in Condado.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 22-year-old woman from Indianapolis, USA, drowned at Condado Beach in San Juan while attempting to rescue two people who had been swept away by a rip current. The incident occurred at approximately 7:00 p.m. on September 8th. Although the two people she was trying to save were rescued, she unfortunately died, and her body was recovered on the afternoon of September 9th.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slowly decaying long-period north northeasterly swell continued to reach the north coast of Puerto Rico. This swell caused high rip current risk and high surf conditions across the local beaches. One person drowned due to rip currents during this event.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 62-year-old male drowned in Terraplen La Posita Beach, road PR-187 in Pinones.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Rough surf and high intensity rip currents along the Lower Texas coast for several days were present when a man ventured into the surf, unaware of the power of the water.  The swimmer, who was from Houston, was quickly moved by the current into deeper water, where he drowned.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A man ventured into rough and confused surf after completing his shift at the Space Exploration Technologies (SpaceX) factory just west of Boca Chica Beach.  The rough surf, which included intense rip currents and surf waves higher than four feet, took the man quickly offshore, where he was unable to return back and disappeared into the sea, according to Cameron County sheriff deputies on-scene. Another man who accompanied the deceased attempted to rescue him, but could not.  Multiple local, state, and federal agencies assisted in the initial search, and the U.S. Coast Guard took over later that day.  A search was called off by the U.S. Coast Guard the following morning due to rough seas.||The body of the deceased was found on Boca Chica Beach nearly 36 hours later.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A high rip current risk continued in the wake of Hurricane Milton with frequent rip currents along the local Atlantic coast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A male drowned in a rip current on Sunday, 10/12 at Mickler's Landing.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A high rip current risk continued in the wake of Hurricane Milton with frequent rip currents along the local Atlantic coast.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Local broadcast media reported that St Johns County Fire Rescue pulled a woman from out of the ocean near the Ponte Vedra Inn and |            Club. The woman was taken to the hospital in |            critical condition.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A couple of water rescues were required at Illinois Lake Michigan beaches on the 18th. One 16 year old boy unfortunately succumbed to the dangerous swimming conditions.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two men were transported to an area hospital after requiring rescue from Lake Michigan at Illinois Beach State Park in Zion. A Beach Hazards Statement was in effect at the time advertising 6 to 10 foot waves and dangerous currents along the Illinois lakeshore.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A surface high pressure across the North Atlantic promoted a moderate to locally fresh easterly wind flow, creating localized choppy conditions. These choppy seas resulted in breaking waves between 3 and 5 feet, increasing the risk to moderate, especially along Jobo's beach, located across northwest PR.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An 83-year-old man (tourist) drowned while swimming at Playa Jobos in Isabela.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The Marianas was under a seasonal trade-wind pattern, with the the primary swell being the trade swell, so highest surf was along east facing reefs and lower along west facing reefs. Rip Currents were likely associated with cuts or channels within the reef, which are know to generate strong currents even when surf is not abnormally high.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Guam Fire Department responded to two kayakers that were distressed at the Hag��t��a Boat Basin Channel around 0913ChST. one man was 55 years old and was unconscious and being assisted by a local surfer. CPR was started and he was transported to Naval Hospital. The second man was 61 years old and was transported to Guam Memorial Hospital with minor injuries. The final condition of the 55-year-old man is currently unknown to the NWS.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The Marianas was under a seasonal trade-wind pattern, with the the primary swell being the trade swell, so highest surf was along east facing reefs and lower along west facing reefs. Rip Currents were likely associated with cuts or channels within the reef, which are know to generate strong currents even when surf is not abnormally high.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Guam Fire Department (GFD) Fire and Water Rescue responded to a report of one distressed swimmer and one snorkeler who was unaccounted for at 1425ChST around First Beach of Ipan, Talo���fo���fo, located on the eastern side of Guam. When Guam Fire and Water Rescue arrived, a 27-year-old man was already brought into shore via bystanders. GFD personnel initiated CPR and the victim was transported to Naval Hospital, while the second victim, a 28-year-old man, was treated for minor injuries on shore and also transported to Naval Hospital. It is believed that the 27-year-old man passed due to drowning as WFO Guam was later contacted for weather and sea information for December 7th, regarding a drowning of a service member, which was near the location of where the 27 year-old-man was pulled from the water.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A kayak capsized off the east coast of Ngaraard, Palau near the village of Elab. Strong currents within Ngedub Channel pulled the fisherman out into the open ocean.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: According to a news article in the Islands Times, a newspaper in Palau, two men from Ngaraard went fishing of the east side of island when their kayak overturned Some time after noon. One man, 32 years old, was swept out to sea, while the other, age not given, grabbed onto a buoy within the channel. The man who grabbed the buoy eventually decided not to fight the strong currents and drifted out of channel, but later was swept back over the reef and he was able to get back to shore early in the evening. The 32 year old man was never found and assumed lost. Altimetry and buoy data near Palau reported seas around 7 to 8 feet with a mixed east swell and secondary NNW swell.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A trade-wind surge east of the Marianas and near the northern Marshall Islands, generated a elevated trade swell that increased surf and the risk of rip currents along eastern shores of the Marianas. Some of the strongest rip currents typically occur along cuts or channels within the reef. This can create dangerous conditions for swimmers, or people on personal craft such as paddleboards and kayaks.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Guam fire Department (GFD) Fire and Water Rescue rescued two fishermen that were trapped in the Togcha Channel around 1930ChST, located behind Jeff's Priates Cove in the beach side area known as Ipan within the village of Talo���fo���fo. Both fishermen made it back to shore with the assistance of GFD personnel and refused all medical services.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Pulses of northerly swells moving across the local waters, along with fresh to locally strong easterly winds, promoted hazardous coastal conditions for the local islands. Exposed coastal areas, including Culebra, had a High Risk of Rip Currents due to breaking waves between 6 to 8 feet. A rip current related death occurred in Culebra.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 68-year-old man from Connecticut, a resident of Culebra, was last seen being dragged by a rip current at Flamenco Beach, Culebra. His body was found after two days.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: On Christmas Day, a high risk of rip currents was in effect for northern Puerto Rico until 6 PM AST (becoming moderate after) due to increased winds and breaking waves around 6 feet. Unfortunately, under these hazardous coastal conditions a rip current related fatality was reported in Luquillo.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 90-year-old resident in Luquillo and a visitor from Utah, USA, was found dead, likely due to drowning, approximately 30 miles offshore from Costa Azul in Luquillo. The incident occurred around 5 PM AST on Christmas Day, and Emergency Managers initiated the search and rescue mission with the US Coast Guard after he was reported missing at 9:30 PM. According to reports from Luquillo's Emergency Management director and the US Coast Guard, it is believed that he died after being caught in a rip current that dragged him out to sea.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A long period northerly swell created hazardous coastal conditions along the north-facing beaches of PR and the US Virgin Islands during the third weekend of November. The exposed Atlantic coastline were  impacted by breaking waves between 8 and 15 feet. Additionally, the full moon phase exacerbated conditions, with isolated coastal flooding along the most vulnerable beaches of northern PR. Coastal Flood Advisories, High Surf Advisories and High Risk of Rip Currents were in effect. One rip current related drowning occurred in Arecibo.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 40-year-old male tourist from Michigan drowned at La Cueva del Indio, near road PR-681 in the Islote sector of Arecibo. According to reports, he was caught in a rip        current.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure over the Atlantic Ocean brought moderate onshore winds to the coast of Palm Beach County in South Florida, which led to strong rip currents and rough surf on November 6, 2024. Large breaking waves, up to 8 feet, in the surf zone resulted in dangerous beach conditions.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast media reported that a 50-year-old Canadian man died after a strong rip current pulled him away from a friend while the pair swam off Ocean Ridge. The persistent moderate easterly flow resulted in a high risk of rip currents for the Palm Beach County beaches. Time is estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure over the Atlantic Ocean brought moderate onshore winds to the coast of Palm Beach County in South Florida, which led to strong rip currents and rough surf on November 2nd and 3rd. Large breaking waves in the surf zone resulted in dangerous beach conditions.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Local broadcast media reported, and Palm Beach Medical Examiner's office confirmed, that a 64-year-old man died in at a Singer Island beach when drowning due to strong rip currents. The persistent moderate easterly flow resulted in a high risk of rip currents and dangerous surf for the Palm Beach County beaches. Time is estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure over the Atlantic Ocean brought moderate onshore winds to the coast of Palm Beach County in South Florida, which led to strong rip currents and rough surf on November 2nd and 3rd. Large breaking waves in the surf zone resulted in dangerous beach conditions.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Local broadcast media and Palm Beach Sheriff's Office reported that the Manalapan Police Department received a 911 call from a beachgoer reporting a swimmer in distress just north of the Boynton Inlet. Security officers and medics from a nearby estate rescued a man from the rough surf and rip currents, administering CPR until Palm Beach County Fire Rescue personnel arrived. The swimmer was taken to a local hospital where he was pronounced dead by emergency room staff at 11:17am.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A 16-year-old male from Fort Pierce drowned after being caught in a rip current at Pepper Park Beach.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 16-year-old male was pulled from the surf at Pepper Park Beach in Fort Pierce, FL on Sunday, November 3, 2024 around 6:00 p.m. in the evening. He was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital where he died later that evening. The beach is typically guarded through the day, until about 5:00 p.m. The threat of rip currents was high that day, and witnesses indicated that rough surf was occurring at the time of the incident.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Rip currents within the western reefs of Guam led to dangerous swimming/wading conditions, leading to the death of a fisherman.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Guam Fire Department's water rescue team responded to Family Beach at 1700ChST when they received a reported of a overdue fisherman. Family Beach is located near the village of Piti, and is on a narrow strip of land that extends westward from Piti and the south side of the strip forms the northern boundary of Apra Harbor, while the northern side faces the Philippine Sea. Jointed by U.S. Coast Guard and Helicopter Sea Combat Squadron 25, crews searched until sunset Saturday and then resumed the search 0700ChST Sunday. At 0753ChST fire department rescue divers eventually located the body of the 24-year-old fisherman about 50 feet below the surface.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure over the Atlantic Ocean brought moderate onshore winds to the coast of Palm Beach County in South Florida, which led to strong rip currents on November 10, 2024.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast media reported one fatality of a 15 year old child who was caught in a strong rip current near Gulf Stream Park in Boynton Beach. Two other family members were rescued. The persistent moderate easterly flow resulted in a high risk of rip |currents for the Palm Beach County beaches. Time is estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High pressure over the Atlantic Ocean brought moderate onshore winds to the coast of Palm Beach County in South Florida, which led to strong rip currents on November 10, 2024.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast media reported one fatality of a 55 year old man who was caught in a strong rip current when swimming at a resort in Palm Beach. Two people responded when the man was heard yelling and brought to shore. Local rescue crews tried to revive the man and were unsuccessful. Red flags were flying at the resort next door due to a high risk of rip currents and unsafe swimming conditions for the Palm Beach County beaches. Time is estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Locally generated rip currents on a low-risk day caused a drowning in Isabela.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A tourist drowned at Shacks Beach in Isabela after being swept away by rip currents while snorkeling.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Long period swell energy, high surf and modest east to northeast winds led to conditions favorable for strong rip currents along the Southeast South Carolina beaches.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Hilton Head Island Beach Patrol reported an adult male fatality near 21 Dune Lane due to a large set of waves pulling the individual back into the water and behind the breakers where a strong rip formed.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Long period swell energy, high surf and modest east to northeast winds led to conditions favorable for strong rip currents along the Southeast South Carolina beaches.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The Hilton Head Island Beach Patrol reported an adult male fatality near 7 Ketch Lane due to large breaking waves and a strong rip current.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A long period northerly swell produced large breaking waves and strong rip currents along the northern beaches of the islands late in December. On the 28th, a person drowned after getting caught in a rip current in Loiza, PR.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The police marine unit and emergency managers reported that a 39-year-old man drowned after being caught in a rip current behind Mar-Bella Restaurant in Loiza. A woman was also swept by the rip current at the same location but was successfully rescued by the first responders.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Hazardous beach conditions developed just before Christmas along the Atlantic beaches of South Florida due to a onshore wind flow and swell from the open Atlantic.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Broadcast media relayed reports of a 48-year-old man rescued by Palm Beach County Ocean Rescue near Carlin Park in Jupiter. The swimmer became distressed after becoming caught in a rip current.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Galveston Beach Patrol rescued a swimmer from a rip current.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Galveston Beach Patrol rescued 1 female from a rip current near the west side of tower 33.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A long period northerly swell produced high surf and life-threatening rip currents along the northern coast of the islands during the last weekend of February.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 62-year-old man drowned while trying to rescue a female with two of his friends in Vacia Talega Beach.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A fading northerly swell and breezy to locally windy conditions promoted life-threatening rip currents for the northern coast of Puerto Rico, among other areas, on January 19th. A high risk of rip currents was in effect for northern Puerto Rico, due to breaking waves of around 6 feet. A rip current related death occurred in Arecibo before sunrise on January 19th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A 63-year-old man was fishing with his son at a boat ramp near Playa Abacoa, close to the mouth of Ca��o Tiburones in Arecibo. At approximately 5:40 AM AST, the man lost his footing and fell into the water, where strong rip currents swiftly carried him into open waters. His son immediately alerted emergency services, leading to a rapid mobilization of local resources, including the U.S. Coast Guard. Later that day, his shoe and baseball cap were discovered approximately a mile and a half offshore. The search efforts continued until the afternoon of January 20 (the following day), when his body was found near Club Nautico de Arecibo at around 3 PM.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Adelup Point is located on the western side of Guam with its reef exposed to the north and west swells. Within the reef, especially on the north side of Adelup, water levels become shallow during low tide and give for easier access to the reefs and cuts in the reef.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Guam Fire Department rescue units responded to a report of a missing spear fisherman at the right side (north side) of Adelup. GFD rescuers conducted a surface water search along the reef line and located the missing spear fisherman. The 32-year-old man was found unconscious and unresponsive and CPR was conducted as he has brought to the Hag��t��a marina via GFD rescue boat. CPR was terminated by GFD paramedics based on medial control methods.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Drowning occurred early in the morning as a result of a rip current.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: First responders received a report of a lost swimmer around 12:45 AM CDT early Wednesday morning, whom had been swimming on the eastern side of the 24th Street Jetty in the no swimming zone. Beach patrol indicated that the swimmer had been seen being pulled out to sea, likely the result of a rip current. EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A long-period northerly swell impacted the Atlantic waters and northern coastal areas of Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands from February 18 through February 20, 2026. The swell propagated across the regional waters, producing increasing wave heights and hazardous marine conditions.||Breaking waves initially ranged from 6 to 8 feet and increased to between 10 and 12 feet as the event intensified. These conditions generated high surf and life-threatening rip currents along north- to northeast-facing beaches, including Puerto Rico, Culebra, and the northern U.S. Virgin Islands.||The most hazardous conditions occurred from February 19 to 20, when the combination of long-period swell and elevated wave energy led to dangerous coastal conditions. Impacts gradually diminished after February 20 as the swell subsided.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A rip current incident occurred at Puerto Nuevo Beach in Vega Baja during the morning of February 19, 2026. Four individuals entered the water and were swept toward deeper waters by a strong rip current. Three individuals returned safely to shore, while one was carried offshore. Search efforts continued for more than a week; however, the individual was not recovered and was classified as missing and presumed dead. This fatality was attributed to hazardous marine conditions associated with a long-period northerly swell.
